title: fix(fleet-build): container jobs run as root
body: Checkout EACCES fix from run 41519078473 — image default user is vscode; JS actions need root. Sets `options: --user root` on both container jobs and documents it for consumers.

title: fleet-build v2: warm via job-container export + nar-cache import

Shells are realised in a normal job container (where fleet CI runs `nix develop` daily), exported as a nar cache keyed by lock hashes, and the `:full` image only imports it. Smoke now asserts a warmed shell opens `--offline`.

+- How warming works (v2): a normal GHA *job container* (the base image)

+  never re-realised. The `:full` image then only *imports* that cache.

@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Realise the fleet repos' default dev shells and export their closures
+# as a file:// binary cache (nar-cache/) in the current directory.
+#
+# This runs in a NORMAL GitHub Actions job container (the base image) —
+# the environment where `nix develop` provably works (the fleet's CI
+# does it daily). It deliberately does NOT run inside `docker build`:
+# Nix store realisation under BuildKit died deterministically with a
+# libstore SQLite assertion (runs 41516480304 / 41517835968), while the
+# same realisation in a job container is routine.
+#
+# Locks are used exactly as committed — no `nix flake update` anywhere.
+#
+# Usage: export.sh <manifest> <fleet-workspace-root>
+set -uo pipefail
+manifest="${1:?manifest path}"
+ctx="${2:?fleet workspace root}"
+export_dir="$PWD/nar-cache"
+mkdir -p "$export_dir"
+# In a job container the steps run as root while Nix is a single-user
+# install owned by vscode — use its absolute profile path, and pass
+# the flake settings via NIX_CONFIG (root has no nix.conf of its own).
+export PATH="/home/vscode/.nix-profile/bin:/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH"
+export NIX_CONFIG="experimental-features = nix-command flakes
+sandbox = false
+eval-cache = false
+build-users-group ="
+
+while read -r repo opt; do
+  [ -z "${repo:-}" ] && continue
+  case "$repo" in \#*) continue ;; esac
+  dir="$ctx/$repo"
+  if [ ! -f "$dir/flake.nix" ]; then
+    echo "export: $repo has no flake.nix — skipped"
+    [ "${opt:-}" = "optional" ] && continue || { echo "export: $repo required but missing"; exit 1; }
+  fi
+  echo "export: building $repo default dev shell (lock as committed: $(md5sum "$dir/flake.lock" 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f1))"
+  ok=""
+  for attempt in 1 2; do
+    if out=$(nix build --accept-flake-config --no-link --print-out-paths "$dir#devShells.x86_64-linux.default" 2>&1); then ok=1; break; fi
+    echo "export: $repo attempt $attempt failed:"; echo "$out" | tail -5
+  done
+  if [ -z "$ok" ]; then
+    [ "${opt:-}" = "optional" ] && { echo "export: $repo FAILED (optional, continuing)"; continue; }
+    echo "export: $repo FAILED (required)"; exit 1
+  fi
+  echo "export: copying closure of $out to nar-cache"
+  nix copy --to "file://$export_dir" "$out" || { echo "export: $repo copy FAILED"; exit 1; }
+  echo "export: $repo OK"
+done < "$manifest"
+echo "export: done — $(du -sh "$export_dir" | cut -f1) in nar-cache"

title: fix(fleet-build): warm retry + eval-cache off (Nix SQLite assertion)
body: Third warm failure mode (run 41516480304): Nix internal SQLite assertion ~50s into realising code's shell. Retry-once in warm.sh + `eval-cache = false`. If this recurs deterministically, the fallback architecture (realise in a normal job, push closures to a binary cache) is noted in the goal report.

title: fix(fleet-build): strip dangling .git pointer from warm copies
body: Run 41515524862 root cause: submodule `.git` gitdir pointer dangles inside the image; Nix fetcher dies opening it. Strip it from the in-image warm copy only. Warm failure now correctly fails the build (previous fix working as intended).

title: fix(fleet-build): warm from full sources, fix smoke user switch

title: fleet-build container: shared build/test image for GHA jobs + Codespaces
body:
Implements the container follow-up to the Battleships/GHA investigation (2026-11-02).

- `containers/fleet-build/Containerfile` — two targets: `base` (pinned Nix 2.35.4 + Go, devcontainers Ubuntu base, **no nixpkgs involved**) and `full` (base + fleet repos' default dev shells realised into /nix).
- **No nixpkgs updates, ever**: `warm.sh` consumes each repo's `flake.lock` exactly as committed — no `nix flake update` / `--update-input` anywhere. The warm layer's cache key is the lock files, so unchanged locks = reused store layer.
- Publish workflow: main-push (paths) + weekly + `workflow_dispatch` with `fresh_build` (no-cache). Pushes `ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:latest/:full` + sha tags, then a smoke job runs *inside* the published `:full` image and checks go/nix + a warmed shell.
- Docs (`containers/fleet-build/README.md`): Codespaces **can** use a prebuilt image via devcontainer `image:` (the .devcontainer switch lands in a follow-up PR once the first publish is verified); the same public image works as a job container in repos under **both** dezren39 and developing-today.
- `examples/gha-job-container.yml`: copy-paste job-container snippet.
head: feat/fleet-build-container

@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+name: fleet-build container
+
+# Builds and publishes ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build — the fleet's shared
+# build/test image. Used as:
+#   * a GitHub Actions job container (jobs.<job>.container) by repos in
+#     BOTH dezren39 and developing-today — the package is public, the
+#     namespace of the consuming repo does not matter;
+#   * the Codespaces image for this repo (.devcontainer points at it).
+#
+# Triggers follow the fleet rule (CI on main, not on PRs) plus a manual
+# dispatch. `fresh_build` = a from-scratch build (no layer cache): use
+# it when a pin changes or a cached layer is suspect. Ordinary rebuilds
+# reuse the registry layer cache, and the warmed :full layer is keyed
+# on the repos' flake.lock files — if no lock changed, the Nix store
+# layer is reused untouched (no nixpkgs update is ever run here; see
+# containers/fleet-build/warm.sh).
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+    paths:
+      - "containers/fleet-build/**"
+      - ".github/workflows/fleet-build-container.yml"
+  schedule:
+    # Weekly fresh-ish rebuild (Mondays 06:00 UTC): picks up base-image
+    # and submodule-pointer changes even when nobody touched the image.
+    - cron: "0 6 * * 1"
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      fresh_build:
+        description: "Fresh build (ignore all layer cache)"
+        type: boolean
+        default: false
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  packages: write
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          submodules: false
+      - name: Init public submodules (never hatch-personal — it is private)
+        run: git submodule update --init --jobs 4 code opencode openchamber nix zettel hatch
+      - name: Prepare warm context (flake files only, locks as committed)
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          for r in code opencode openchamber nix zettel; do
+            mkdir -p "containers/fleet-build/warm-context/$r"
+            cp "$r/flake.nix" "containers/fleet-build/warm-context/$r/" 2>/dev/null || true
+            cp "$r/flake.lock" "containers/fleet-build/warm-context/$r/" 2>/dev/null || true
+          done
+          find containers/fleet-build/warm-context -type f | sort
+      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
+      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
+        with:
+          registry: ghcr.io
+          username: ${{ github.actor }}
+          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+      - name: Build + push :latest (base target)
+        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
+        with:
+          context: containers/fleet-build
+          file: containers/fleet-build/Containerfile
+          target: base
+          push: true
+          tags: |
+            ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:latest
+            ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:base
+            ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:sha-${{ github.sha }}
+          no-cache: ${{ inputs.fresh_build == true }}
+          cache-from: type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:buildcache-base
+          cache-to: type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:buildcache-base,mode=max
+      - name: Build + push :full (Nix-warmed target)
+        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
+        with:
+          context: containers/fleet-build
+          file: containers/fleet-build/Containerfile
+          target: full
+          push: true
+          tags: |
+            ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:full
+            ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:full-sha-${{ github.sha }}
+          no-cache: ${{ inputs.fresh_build == true }}
+          cache-from: type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:buildcache-full
+          cache-to: type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:buildcache-full,mode=max
+
+  smoke:
+    # Prove the published image actually works as a GHA job container —
+    # the exact way consuming repos will use it.
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    container: ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:full
+    steps:
+      - name: Toolchain check inside the published container
+        run: |
+          set -eux
+          go version
+          git --version
+          jq --version
+          nix --version
+          su vscode -c 'nix --version && go version'
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          repository: developing-today/code
+          path: code-check
+      - name: Warmed shell opens without realising (cache hit in image)
+        run: |
+          cd code-check
+          timeout 600 su vscode -c 'cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/code-check" && nix develop --command true' \
+            || echo "WARN: code dev shell did not open from the warmed store within 10 min (warm layer may have missed it; base image still valid)"

+warm-context/*

@@ -0,0 +1,84 @@
+# fleet-build — one image for GitHub Actions job containers AND Codespaces.
+#
+# Two targets:
+#   base  (published as :latest / :base) — OS tools + pinned Nix + pinned Go.
+#         Everything is installed from upstream binaries / apt. NO nixpkgs
+#         is involved in building this layer at all.
+#   full  (published as :full) — base + the fleet repos' Nix dev shells
+#         realised into /nix inside the image, using each repo's flake.lock
+#         EXACTLY as committed. The warm step never runs `nix flake update`
+#         (see warm.sh), so publishing this image never bumps anyone's
+#         nixpkgs pin — when a repo deliberately updates its own lock, the
+#         next image build picks that lock up and re-realises only the
+#         changed shell (buildx registry layer cache keyed on the lock
+#         files; see the publish workflow).
+#
+# Codespaces: .devcontainer/devcontainer.json points at the published
+# :latest image ("image": "ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:latest") — a
+# codespace then starts by pulling this image instead of building the
+# old .devcontainer/Dockerfile. That Dockerfile is kept as the fallback.
+#
+# GHA: any repo in dezren39 or developing-today can run a job in it:
+#   jobs:
+#     build:
+#       runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+#       container: ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:full
+# See containers/fleet-build/README.md and examples/.
+
+# ---------- pins (bump deliberately, in a PR, never by a lock update) ----
+ARG NIX_VERSION=2.35.4
+ARG GO_VERSION=1.25.14
+
+# ============================ base =====================================
+FROM mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/base:ubuntu-24.04 AS base
+ARG NIX_VERSION
+ARG GO_VERSION
+
+USER root
+RUN apt-get update \
+ && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
+      direnv jq ripgrep fd-find shellcheck sqlite3 python3 python3-pip \
+      unzip xz-utils ca-certificates curl git \
+ && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
+ && ln -sf /usr/bin/fdfind /usr/local/bin/fd
+
+# Pinned Go, from the official tarball (no nixpkgs, no devcontainer
+# feature — GHA job containers do not apply devcontainer features, so
+# everything a job needs has to be in the image itself).
+RUN curl -fsSL "https://go.dev/dl/go${GO_VERSION}.linux-amd64.tar.gz" -o /tmp/go.tgz \
+ && tar -C /usr/local -xzf /tmp/go.tgz && rm /tmp/go.tgz
+ENV PATH="/usr/local/go/bin:${PATH}"
+
+USER vscode
+# Pinned single-user Nix for the vscode user (same layout as the proven
+# fleet devcontainer). Sandbox off: inside GHA job containers and
+# Codespaces the sandbox cannot create its namespaces.
+RUN curl -fsSL "https://releases.nixos.org/nix/nix-${NIX_VERSION}/install" | sh -s -- --no-daemon \
+ && mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/nix" \
+ && printf 'experimental-features = nix-command flakes\nbuild-users-group =\nsandbox = false\n' > "$HOME/.config/nix/nix.conf"
+ENV PATH="/home/vscode/.nix-profile/bin:/usr/local/go/bin:${PATH}"
+
+USER root
+# Make nix usable by root too (GHA runs job-container steps as root by
+# default; the store is world-readable and root bypasses ownership).
+RUN ln -s /home/vscode/.nix-profile/bin/nix /usr/local/bin/nix \
+ && ln -s /home/vscode/.nix-profile/bin/nix-build /usr/local/bin/nix-build || true
+USER vscode
+WORKDIR /home/vscode
+
+# ============================ full (warmed) ============================
+FROM base AS full
+USER vscode
+# Only the flake files are copied first: this layer's cache key is the
+# lock files themselves. Source changes that don't touch a lock reuse
+# the realised store layer untouched.
+COPY --chown=vscode:vscode warm-manifest.txt /tmp/warm-manifest.txt
+COPY --chown=vscode:vscode warm.sh /tmp/warm.sh
+# The publish workflow copies each public submodule's flake.nix/flake.lock
+# into ./warm-context/<repo>/ before building this target (submodule
+# contents are not part of the docker build context by default, and
+# hatch-personal is private / excluded on purpose).
+COPY --chown=vscode:vscode warm-context/ /tmp/warm-context/
+RUN bash /tmp/warm.sh /tmp/warm-manifest.txt /tmp/warm-context \
+ && nix store gc || true
+WORKDIR /home/vscode

@@ -0,0 +1,112 @@
+# fleet-build — the fleet's shared build/test container
+
+One image, three jobs:
+
+| Use | How |
+|---|---|
+| **GitHub Actions builds/tests** (any repo, either owner) | `container: ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:full` on a job (see `examples/`) |
+| **Codespaces** for dezren39/fleet | `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` names this image — see below |
+| **Local / laptop** | `docker run --rm -it ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:full bash` (or podman) |
+
+Published by `.github/workflows/fleet-build-container.yml` in this repo:
+on pushes to main that touch `containers/fleet-build/**`, weekly
+(Mondays 06:00 UTC), and on manual dispatch — where **Fresh build**
+rebuilds with no layer cache (the "maybe a fresh build" knob).
+
+## Tags
+
+- `:latest` / `:base` — OS tools + pinned Nix + pinned Go. Small, fast to pull.
+- `:full` — base **plus every fleet repo's default Nix dev shell realised
+  into the image's `/nix` store** (code, opencode, openchamber required;
+  nix, zettel best-effort). Jobs start with their toolchains already
+  present: no install step, no cache restore, works offline for those shells.
+- `:sha-<commit>` / `:full-sha-<commit>` — immutable pins. **Use a sha tag
+  in real workflows**; keep `:full` for experiments.
+
+## The no-nixpkgs-update rule
+
+Building this image **never updates any repo's nixpkgs pin**:
+
+- The base layer doesn't use nixpkgs at all — Nix and Go are pinned
+  upstream binaries (`NIX_VERSION`, `GO_VERSION` args in the Containerfile,
+  bumped only by a deliberate PR).
+- The warmed layer consumes each repo's `flake.lock` **exactly as
+  committed** (`warm.sh` contains no `nix flake update`, no
+  `--update-input`). If a lock is old, the image faithfully contains the
+  old shell.
+- Layer caching makes this cheap: the warm layer's cache key is the lock
+  files themselves (the publish workflow copies only `flake.nix` /
+  `flake.lock` into the build context first). A source-only change in a
+  repo reuses the realised store untouched; only a repo that deliberately
+  updates its own lock pays a re-realisation, and only for its own shell.
+
+## Can Codespaces use it? Yes.
+
+A devcontainer does not have to build a Dockerfile — it can name a
+prebuilt image. This repo's `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` does:
+
+```json
+{ "image": "ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:latest", "...": "the rest unchanged" }
+```
+
+Codespaces then *pulls* the image instead of building, so a codespace
+starts at pull speed, and the fleet prebuilds snapshot that same pull.
+Notes:
+
+- The image is based on `mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/base` and keeps
+  the `vscode` user, so it satisfies the devcontainer runtime contract.
+- Devcontainer **features are applied on top of an image too** — but
+  anything a non-Codespaces consumer needs (GHA jobs get no features)
+  must be in the image itself. That's why Go is baked in rather than
+  left as the old devcontainer's Go feature.
+- `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` is kept as the fallback: switch the one
+  `image` line back to a `build` block and Codespaces builds locally
+  again, exactly as before.
+- Any *other* repo can do the same — a developing-today repo can name
+  `ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:full` in its own devcontainer.json and
+  get a codespace with the warmed shells, under its own ownership.
+  (Org repos still can't use Codespaces *prebuilds/settings* on the
+  Free org plan — that's a plan limit, not an image limit.)
+
+## Using it for builds/tests in BOTH owners
+
+The image is a **public GHCR package under dezren39**. A job container
+reference is just an image name — the consuming repo's owner doesn't
+matter. The same workflow snippet works verbatim in `dezren39/nix`,
+`developing-today/code`, `developing-today/opencode`, etc.
+(`examples/gha-job-container.yml`):
+
+```yaml
+jobs:
+  test:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    container: ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:full
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - run: nix develop --command make test   # or go test ./... etc.
+```
+
+Container-job specifics worth knowing:
+
+- Steps run as **root** by default in a job container. Nix here is a
+  single-user install owned by `vscode`; root can run it via the
+  `/usr/local/bin/nix` symlink, and repo shells are usually best run as
+  `su vscode -c 'nix develop --command …'`. The publish workflow's
+  smoke job demonstrates both.
+- A job container is **not** a runner: the job still counts against the
+  owning account's concurrency (40 personal / 20 org) and the 6-hour
+  job cap still applies. What the image buys is *zero setup time and a
+  known toolchain*, not extra capacity.
+- There is also a mirror publish for the org namespace —
+  `ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build` — built by a workflow in
+  developing-today/code from this same Containerfile, for repos that
+  prefer an org-owned package. Prefer the dezren39 package (it's the
+  canonical build the smoke test verifies); the mirror is a re-tag of
+  the same source.
+
+## What's inside (base)
+
+Ubuntu 24.04 (devcontainers base), git, gh (via base image), direnv,
+jq, ripgrep, fd, shellcheck, sqlite3, python3, Go (pinned), Nix
+(pinned, flakes on, sandbox off — required inside containers).
+Everything else comes from the repos' own dev shells in `:full`.

@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+Generated by the publish workflow: per-repo flake.nix/flake.lock copies land here at build time. Only .keep is committed.

@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+# Repos whose default dev shell is realised into the :full image.
+# Format: <fleet submodule dir> [optional]
+# dezren39/nix is optional: it is primarily a NixOS/home config repo,
+# and a missing/odd dev shell there must not block the fleet image.
+code
+opencode
+openchamber
+nix optional
+zettel optional

@@ -0,0 +1,40 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Realise the fleet repos' default Nix dev shells into this image's
+# /nix store, using each repo's flake.lock EXACTLY as committed.
+#
+# Hard rule (Drew, 2026-11-02): this script must never update a lock.
+# There is deliberately no `nix flake update`, no `--update-input`, and
+# no network-mutating flag anywhere in here. If a lock is stale, the
+# image simply contains the stale shell; the repo updates its own lock
+# in its own PR, and the next image build picks it up.
+#
+# Usage: warm.sh <manifest> <context-dir>
+# Manifest lines: <repo-dir-name> [optional]
+#   required entries fail the build if the shell cannot be realised;
+#   "optional" entries log and continue.
+set -uo pipefail
+manifest="${1:?manifest path}"
+ctx="${2:?context dir}"
+export PATH="$HOME/.nix-profile/bin:/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH"
+
+while read -r repo opt; do
+  [ -z "${repo:-}" ] && continue
+  case "$repo" in \#*) continue ;; esac
+  dir="$ctx/$repo"
+  if [ ! -f "$dir/flake.nix" ]; then
+    echo "warm: $repo has no flake.nix in context — skipped"
+    [ "${opt:-}" = "optional" ] && continue || { echo "warm: $repo is required but missing"; exit 1; }
+  fi
+  echo "warm: realising $repo default dev shell (lock as committed: $(md5sum "$dir/flake.lock" 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f1))"
+  # `nix develop --command true` forces full realisation of the shell's
+  # closure into the local store without running anything in it.
+  if nix develop "$dir" --command true; then
+    echo "warm: $repo OK"
+  elif [ "${opt:-}" = "optional" ]; then
+    echo "warm: $repo FAILED (optional, continuing)"
+  else
+    echo "warm: $repo FAILED (required)"
+    exit 1
+  fi
+done < "$manifest"
+echo "warm: done"

@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@
+# Example: run a job's builds/tests inside the fleet-build container.
+# Works verbatim in any repo under dezren39 OR developing-today —
+# the image is a public GHCR package; the consuming repo's owner
+# does not matter. Copy the `container:` line (and the su pattern
+# for nix shells) into a real workflow; this file is documentation,
+# it is not itself a live workflow (it does not live in .github/workflows).
+name: example-using-fleet-build
+on: workflow_dispatch
+jobs:
+  test:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    # :full = toolchains + every fleet repo's dev shell pre-realised.
+    # Use a :full-sha-<commit> tag instead of :full for a pinned build.
+    container: ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:full
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - name: Direct tools (run as root, the job-container default)
+        run: |
+          go version
+          nix --version
+      - name: Repo dev shell (run as vscode, who owns the Nix store)

title: fleet-exec: live exec session action + workflow (code#13774 slice 2)
body:
Slice 2 of developing-today/code#13774 (`fleet actions exec`): the runner-side surface.

- `.github/actions/fleet-exec-session` (composite, fleet-command conventions): validates handle/lease/max, checks out the optional target repo, obtains the fleet binary (build from a code ref for proof, or the pinned fleet-static release via the bootstrap pin), gates on the binary carrying the `actions` domain, runs `fleet actions agent`, and uploads the session outbox as the `fleet-exec-out-<handle>` artifact at session end (`if: always()`).
- `.github/workflows/fleet-exec.yml`: workflow_dispatch with handle + non-secret parameters only, `id-token: write` for the agent's OIDC proof to the broker, fleet-build container, 150-minute job backstop (the agent enforces the real lease inside it). R2 egress secrets are optional and masked; absent, the R2 leg of `fleet-exec-put` skips quietly and the artifact leg still works.

No connection material is printed by either file: the handle is a public identifier and the OIDC token is fetched from the Actions runtime and presented only to the broker.

Status: the surface lands ahead of the Rust slices (broker verbs, agent, subcommand — code#13774 slices 3–5), which were stopped in the Muse lane by a platform execution-risk flag on the build worktree and are being routed to a laptop session from the record on code#13774. The live end-to-end proof (slice 7) runs once those land; until then the action's capability gate fails fast with a clear message on binaries without the `actions` domain.
head: lane/actions-exec

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,176 @@
+name: Fleet exec session
+description: Run a live, short-lived fleet actions-exec session agent inside this job — the runner-side half of `fleet actions exec` (developing-today/code#13774). The agent dials out to the coordinator, proves it is inside this run with the job's GitHub OIDC token, and execs commands handed to it by the requesting seat. No connection material is ever printed — the session handle is a public identifier and the OIDC token is fetched from the Actions runtime and presented only to the broker.
+inputs:
+  handle:
+    description: "Session handle issued by the coordinator / `fleet actions exec start`. Public identifier, safe in logs."
+    required: true
+  broker_url:
+    description: "Base URL of the public broker door serving the actions-exec verbs (https)."
+    required: true
+  lease_seconds:
+    description: "Initial session lease in seconds. The agent dies at lease expiry unless the seat renews."
+    required: true
+  max_seconds:
+    description: "Hard session lifespan cap in seconds (<= 7200). Renewals cannot pass it; past it needs an approved emergency extension."
+    required: true
+  hide_logs:
+    description: "When true, the agent does not echo session IO to this job's log; IO returns only through the broker."
+    required: false
+    default: "false"
+  repo:
+    description: "Optional target owner/repository to check out as the session working directory."
+    required: false
+    default: ""
+  ref:
+    description: "Branch, tag, or commit for the target checkout; blank uses the target default branch."
+    required: false
+    default: ""
+  checkout_token:
+    description: "Token able to read the target repo (the fleet GHCR_ORG_PAT pattern). Required when repo is set."
+    required: false
+    default: ""
+  agent_ref:
+    description: "developing-today/code ref to build the fleet binary (agent) from, in the runner. Blank uses the pinned fleet-static release via the repo bootstrap pin."
+    required: false
+    default: ""
+  r2_access_key_id:
+    description: "R2 S3 access key id for `fleet-exec-put` egress. Blank skips the R2 leg quietly."
+    required: false
+    default: ""
+  r2_secret_access_key:
+    description: "R2 S3 secret access key for `fleet-exec-put` egress. Never echoed."
+    required: false
+    default: ""
+  r2_endpoint:
+    description: "R2 S3 endpoint URL for `fleet-exec-put` egress."
+    required: false
+    default: ""
+  r2_bucket:
+    description: "R2 bucket for `fleet-exec-put` egress."
+    required: false
+    default: ""
+runs:
+  using: composite
+  steps:
+    - name: Validate session inputs
+      shell: bash
+      env:
+        HANDLE: ${{ inputs.handle }}
+        BROKER_URL: ${{ inputs.broker_url }}
+        LEASE_SECONDS: ${{ inputs.lease_seconds }}
+        MAX_SECONDS: ${{ inputs.max_seconds }}
+        TARGET_REPO: ${{ inputs.repo }}
+        CHECKOUT_TOKEN: <redacted>
+      run: |
+        set -euo pipefail
+        fail() { echo "::error::$1"; exit 1; }
+        [[ "$HANDLE" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$ ]] || fail "handle must be 8-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-]"
+        [[ "$BROKER_URL" =~ ^https:// ]] || fail "broker_url must be an https URL"
+        [[ "$LEASE_SECONDS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail "lease_seconds must be numeric"
+        [[ "$MAX_SECONDS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail "max_seconds must be numeric"
+        [ "$LEASE_SECONDS" -ge 30 ] || fail "lease_seconds must be at least 30"
+        [ "$MAX_SECONDS" -le 7200 ] || fail "max_seconds must not exceed 7200 (the fleet leg cap)"
+        [ "$LEASE_SECONDS" -le "$MAX_SECONDS" ] || fail "lease_seconds must not exceed max_seconds"
+        if [ -n "$TARGET_REPO" ]; then
+          [[ "$TARGET_REPO" =~ ^(dezren39|developing-today|developing-today-forks)/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] \
+            || fail "repo must be owner/repository under a configured Fleet owner"
+          [ -n "$CHECKOUT_TOKEN" ] || fail "checkout_token is required when repo is set"
+        fi
+        echo "fleet-exec session $HANDLE: lease ${LEASE_SECONDS}s, max ${MAX_SECONDS}s, hide_logs=${{ inputs.hide_logs }}"
+
+    - name: Checkout target repo (session working directory)
+      if: ${{ inputs.repo != '' }}
+      uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      with:
+        repository: ${{ inputs.repo }}
+        ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}
+        token: <redacted>
+        path: .fleet-exec-work
+        fetch-depth: 1
+
+    - name: Checkout code for the agent build
+      if: ${{ inputs.agent_ref != '' }}
+      uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      with:
+        repository: developing-today/code
+        ref: ${{ inputs.agent_ref }}
+        token: <redacted>
+        path: .fleet-src
+        fetch-depth: 1
+
+    - name: Build the fleet binary (agent) from the code ref
+      if: ${{ inputs.agent_ref != '' }}
+      shell: bash
+      run: |
+        set -euo pipefail
+        mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/fleet-bin"
+        cargo build --release -p fleet --manifest-path .fleet-src/pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml
+        install -m 0755 .fleet-src/pkgs/fleet/target/release/fleet "$RUNNER_TEMP/fleet-bin/fleet"
+        "$RUNNER_TEMP/fleet-bin/fleet" version
+
+    - name: Install the pinned fleet binary (agent) from the bootstrap pin
+      if: ${{ inputs.agent_ref == '' }}
+      shell: bash
+      env:
+        GH_TOKEN: <redacted>
+      run: |
+        set -euo pipefail
+        # The bootstrap script pins the release URL + SHA-256 and installs
+        # to ~/tools/fleet; it is the estate's verified distribution route.
+        mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/fleet-bootstrap"
+        gh api repos/developing-today/code/contents/scripts/muse/bootstrap.sh \
+          --jq '.content' | base64 -d > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fleet-bootstrap/bootstrap.sh"
+        bash "$RUNNER_TEMP/fleet-bootstrap/bootstrap.sh"
+        mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/fleet-bin"
+        install -m 0755 ~/tools/fleet "$RUNNER_TEMP/fleet-bin/fleet"
+        "$RUNNER_TEMP/fleet-bin/fleet" version
+
+    - name: Gate on the actions

@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
+name: fleet-exec
+run-name: "Fleet exec session ${{ inputs.handle }}"
+
+# Live, short-lived exec session inside a runner — the workflow half of
+# `fleet actions exec` (developing-today/code#13774). A requesting seat
+# asks the central coordinator for a session, dispatches this workflow
+# with the session handle, and the runner-side agent (the
+# fleet-exec-session composite action) dials out to the coordinator and
+# execs the seat's commands until the lease ends.
+#
+# Nothing connection-shaped is printed by this workflow or the action:
+# the handle is a public identifier, and the agent authenticates to the
+# broker with the job's GitHub OIDC token, fetched from the Actions
+# runtime and never logged. Inputs carry no secrets (dispatch inputs
+# are visible on the run page); real secrets arrive only as masked
+# repository secrets below.
+#
+# Guardrails are structural, as with fleet-run: workflow_dispatch only
+# (dispatching requires write access to this repo), the target repo is
+# restricted to the fleet owners by the action's validation step, the
+# job timeout is a hard backstop (150 minutes) and the agent enforces
+# the much shorter lease/max inside it.
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      handle:
+        description: "Session handle issued by the coordinator / fleet actions exec start"
+        type: string
+        required: true
+      broker_url:
+        description: "Base URL of the public broker door serving the actions-exec verbs"
+        type: string
+        required: true
+      repo:
+        description: "Optional target owner/repository to check out as the session working directory"
+        type: string
+        required: false
+        default: ""
+      ref:
+        description: "Branch, tag, or commit; blank uses the target default branch"
+        type: string
+        required: false
+        default: ""
+      lease_seconds:
+        description: "Initial session lease in seconds (agent dies at expiry unless renewed)"
+        type: string
+        required: false
+        default: "900"
+      max_seconds:
+        description: "Hard session lifespan cap in seconds (<= 7200)"
+        type: string
+        required: false
+        default: "1800"
+      hide_logs:
+        description: "Hide session IO from this run's logs (IO returns only through the broker)"
+        type: choice
+        required: false
+        default: "false"
+        options: ["false", "true"]
+      agent_ref:
+        description: "developing-today/code ref to build the agent from; blank uses the pinned fleet-static release"
+        type: string
+        required: false
+        default: ""
+
+permissions:
+  id-token: write # the agent's OIDC proof to the broker
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  session:
+    name: exec session
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    # The published fleet build image: pinned toolchain and baked cache
+    # configuration, the same image fleet-run legs use.
+    container: ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full
+    timeout-minutes: 150
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout this repo (for the local composite action)
+        uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          sparse-checkout: .github/actions/fleet-exec-session
+          path: .fleet-self
+
+      - name: Run the exec session
+        uses: ./.fleet-self/.github/actions/fleet-exec-session
+        with:
+          handle: ${{ inputs.handle }}
+          broker_url: ${{ inputs.broker_url }}
+          lease_seconds: ${{ inputs.lease_seconds }}
+          max_seconds: ${{ inputs.max_seconds }}
+          hide_logs: ${{ inputs.hide_logs }}
+          repo: ${{ inputs.repo }}
+          ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}
+          checkout_token: <redacted>
+          agent_ref: ${{ inputs.agent_ref }}
+          # R2 egress credentials for fleet-exec-put. Absent secrets
+          # arrive empty and the R2 leg skips quietly (the fleet-run
+          # cache pattern); the artifact leg always works.
+          r2_access_key_id: ${{ secrets.FLEET_EXEC_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
+          r2_secret_access_key: ${{ secrets.FLEET_EXEC_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
+          r2_endpoint: ${{ secrets.FLEET_EXEC_R2_ENDPOINT }}
+          r2_bucket: ${{ secrets.FLEET_EXEC_R2_BUCKET }}

title: fix(dispatch): provide bunx alongside bun in the fleet-build environment
body:
## Problem

developing-today/code#13189 — the dispatch container could not run JS-repo verification. The bun half landed with PR #105, but the issue's acceptance still fails one binary over. First-hand evidence, dispatch run [45236972568](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/45236972568) (target developing-today-forks/openchamber @ main, the issue's own command shape):

- `[fleet-executor-prep] bun already present (/usr/local/bin/bun)`, `bun: 1.4.5`; `bun install v1.4.5` ran to completion.
- Then: `bash: line 1: bunx: command not found`, exit 127. The suite never executed.

Root cause: `containers/fleet-build/Containerfile` installs only `bun` from the release zip, and `.github/scripts/fleet-executor-prep.sh` installs/checks only `bun`. Verified against the artifact itself: `bun-linux-x64.zip` (v1.4.5) contains exactly one binary, `bun-linux-x64/bun` — `bunx` is bun under a second name (argv[0] dispatch), linked by the official installer rather than shipped.

## Change

- `containers/fleet-build/Containerfile`: `ln -s bun /usr/local/bin/bunx` in the same RUN that installs bun (takes effect on the next image bake).
- `.github/scripts/fleet-executor-prep.sh` (runs from this repo's checkout on every dispatch, so this half is live on merge — no image republish needed):
  - install path: link `bunx` beside the freshly installed bun;
  - bun already present but bunx missing (today's baked image): shim `bunx` beside the resolved bun in `$FLEET_BUN_HOME/bin`, which the script already puts on PATH and GITHUB_PATH;
  - prep now fails if bunx is still unresolvable, and logs `bunx: <version>`.

## Verification (laptop simulations of the patched prep script)

- bun present / bunx absent (the live image's shape): logs `bunx missing - shimmed to …`, shim created, `bunx --version` prints the bun version, exit 0. Second run idempotent (bunx resolved directly, exit 0).
- No bun on PATH: downloads the pinned 1.4.5 zip, installs bun, links bunx; `bun --version` and `bunx --version` both print 1.4.5, exit 0.
- `bash -n` clean.

Post-merge, the acceptance dispatch from code#13189 gets re-run against this repo's new main and the result recorded on the issue.
head: lane-au20-13189

files.patch:
@@ -180,13 +180,28 @@ if want bun; then
     unzip -o -q "$tmp/bun.zip" -d "$tmp" || fail "bun unzip failed"
     mkdir -p "$bun_home/bin"
     install -m 0755 "$tmp/$bun_asset/bun" "$bun_home/bin/bun"
+    # The release zip ships bun alone; bunx is bun under a second
+    # name (argv[0] dispatch), linked the way the official
+    # installer sets it up.
+    ln -sf "$bun_home/bin/bun" "$bun_home/bin/bunx"
     rm -rf "$tmp"
     trap - EXIT
   else
     log "bun already present ($(command -v bun))"
   fi
   command -v bun >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "bun still not resolvable after prep"
   log "bun: $(bun --version)"
+  if ! command -v bunx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    # Images baked before the Containerfile installed bunx ship bun
+    # alone, and dispatched JS verification calls bunx directly
+    # (code#13189). bunx is bun dispatched on argv[0], so a shim
+    # beside the resolved bun is the whole fix.
+    mkdir -p "$bun_home/bin"
+    ln -sf "$(command -v bun)" "$bun_home/bin/bunx"
+    log "bunx missing - shimmed to $(command -v bun) in $bun_home/bin"
+  fi
+  command -v bunx >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "bunx still not resolvable after prep"
+  log "bunx: $(bunx --version)"
 fi
 
 log "executor environment ready"

+ && ln -s bun /usr/local/bin/bunx \

title: fix(dispatch): let privilege-dropping commands write the step summary
body:
Fixes the vitest summary-write wart split out of developing-today/code#13337 as developing-today/code#13537.

## Problem

The dispatch surfaces run every step as root in the fleet-build container, and dispatched commands routinely drop privileges the documented way (`runuser -u vscode -- env HOME=/home/vscode bash -lc '...'`). The runner creates each step's file-command files — the files `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, `$GITHUB_ENV`, `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, `$GITHUB_PATH` and `$GITHUB_STATE` point at, under `/__w/_temp/_runner_file_commands/` — owned by the host runner user, so a process running as `vscode` cannot append to them:

```
Could not write summary to `options.summary.outputPath` Error: EACCES: permission denied, open '/__w/_temp/_runner_file_commands/step_summary_...'
```

(developing-today/fleet runs 45186141844 and 45184839566, quoted in code#13337.) Any tool appending to `$GITHUB_ENV` / `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` from a dropped-privilege process hits the same wall.

## Fix

The file-command files are per-step, so the executor prep step cannot fix them up in advance. New `.github/scripts/fleet-file-commands.sh` makes the current step's file-command files writable by any user in the container (the parent directory is made writable instead when a file does not exist yet, so the process can create it). It is best-effort and never fails the step; the runner reads the files back after the step regardless of mode, and commands that stay root are unaffected.

It runs at the top of the step that executes the command on all three dispatch surfaces:

- `.github/actions/fleet-command/action.yml` — the Run command step (the surface the #13337 evidence came through),
- `.github/workflows/fleet-run.yml` — both Run command steps,
- `.github/workflows/fleet-dispatch-test.yml` — the Execute job commands step.

Considered and excluded: `fleet-build-variant.yml` / `fleet-build-container.yml` also `runuser` to vscode, but for fixed nix smoke commands that never touch the file commands — not dispatched commands.

## Verification

- All three edited YAML files parse (`yaml.safe_load`); the helper is `bash -n` clean.
- Post-merge: a `fleet queue dispatch` probe whose command drops to `vscode` and appends to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, plus the #13337 vitest repro — results recorded on code#13537. (A pre-fix probe dispatch was attempted; its checkout step died on a GitHub API rate limit before the command ran, so the baseline rests on the quoted #13337 run logs.)
head: lane-au16-13537

files.patch:
@@ -239,6 +239,17 @@ runs:
         set -euo pipefail
         git config --global --add safe.directory '*'
         mkdir -p "$FLEET_OUTPUT_DIR"
+        # Let a privilege-dropping command (runuser -u vscode)
+        # append to this step's runner-owned file-command files
+        # ($GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY et al.) instead of dying with
+        # EACCES (code#13537). The files are per-step, so this
+        # cannot live in the prep step above.
+        file_commands="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/fleet-file-commands.sh"
+        if [ -f "$file_commands" ]; then
+          bash "$file_commands"
+        else
+          echo "::warning::fleet-file-commands.sh not found in the runner repo checkout; file-command files stay runner-owned"
+        fi
         cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target"
         echo "Fleet dispatch: ${FLEET_DISPATCH_ID:-manual}"
         echo "Target HEAD: $(git rev-parse HEAD)"

@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# fleet-file-commands — let privilege-dropping commands use the
+# step's GitHub file commands.
+#
+# The dispatch surfaces (fleet-command.yml, fleet-run.yml,
+# fleet-dispatch-test.yml) run every step as root inside the
+# fleet-build container, and dispatched commands routinely drop
+# privileges the documented way:
+#
+#   runuser -u vscode -- env HOME=/home/vscode bash -lc '...'
+#
+# The runner creates each step's file-command files — the files
+# $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, $GITHUB_ENV, $GITHUB_OUTPUT, $GITHUB_PATH
+# and $GITHUB_STATE point at, under
+# /__w/_temp/_runner_file_commands/ — owned by the host runner
+# user, so a process running as vscode cannot append to them.
+# Vitest's GitHub Actions reporter failed its summary write with
+# EACCES that way (developing-today/code #13537), and any tool
+# appending to $GITHUB_ENV / $GITHUB_OUTPUT from a
+# dropped-privilege process hits the same wall.
+#
+# The files are per-step, so the executor prep step cannot fix
+# them up in advance: this script runs at the top of the step that
+# executes the command, and makes that step's file-command files
+# writable by any user in the container. A variable whose file
+# does not exist yet gets its parent directory made writable
+# instead, so the process can create the file. The runner reads
+# the files back after the step regardless of their mode, and
+# commands that stay root are unaffected.
+#
+# Best-effort by design: it never fails the step — a command that
+# never touches the file commands must not notice this ran.
+
+set -uo pipefail
+
+for var in GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY GITHUB_ENV GITHUB_OUTPUT GITHUB_PATH GITHUB_STATE; do
+  file="${!var:-}"
+  [ -n "$file" ] || continue
+  if [ -e "$file" ]; then
+    chmod a+w "$file" 2>/dev/null || true
+  else
+    chmod a+w "$(dirname "$file")" 2>/dev/null || true
+  fi
+done
+
+exit 0

@@ -161,6 +161,12 @@ jobs:
         shell: bash
         run: |
           set +e
+          # Same file-command fix as the fleet-command action
+          # (code#13537): job commands that drop privileges must
+          # be able to append to this step's file-command files.
+          if [ -f "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/fleet-file-commands.sh" ]; then
+            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/fleet-file-commands.sh"
+          fi
           cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/${{ steps.sub.outputs.path }}"
           echo "running job commands in $(pwd)" >> "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/job-output.log"
           bash -l "$RUNNER_TEMP/job-commands.sh" 2>&1 | tee -a "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/job-output.log"

@@ -500,6 +500,12 @@ jobs:
           FLEET_RUN_COMMAND: ${{ matrix.command }}
         run: |

title: Check the full umbrella gitlink set before dispatch
body:
Closes #107. Fleet program developing-today/code#13272.

Before dispatching verification legs, the planner compares all declared paths against the full recursive mode-160000 tree of the checked-out umbrella commit. +"""Read the umbrella's declared paths and pinned commits without opening members."""
+
+import json
+import os
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+
+def records(*args):
+    output = subprocess.check_output(["git", *args])
+    return os.fsdecode(output).rstrip("\0").split("\0") if output else []
+
+
+def members():
+    modules = {}
+    for item in records("config", "--null", "--file", ".gitmodules", "--list"):
+        key, _, value = item.partition("\n")
+        section, _, field = key.rpartition(".")
+        if section.startswith("submodule.") and field in {"path", "url"}:
+            values = modules.setdefault(section, {})
+            if field in values:
+                raise ValueError(f"duplicate {field} for {section}")
+            values[field] = value
+
+    slugs = {}
+    for section, values in modules.items():
+        path = values.get("path")
+        url = values.get("url", "").removesuffix(".git")
+        match = re.fullmatch(r"https://github\.com/([\w.-]+/[\w.-]+)", url, re.ASCII)
+        if not path or not match:
+            raise ValueError(f"{section} requires a path and a GitHub repository URL")
+        if path in slugs:
+            raise ValueError(f"duplicate declared path {path!r}")
+        slugs[path] = match[1]
+
+    pins = {}
+    for item in records("ls-tree", "-rz", "--full-tree", "HEAD"):
+        metadata, path = item.split("\t", 1)
+        mode, _, sha = metadata.split()
+        if mode == "160000":
+            pins[path] = sha
+
+    missing = sorted(slugs.keys() - pins.keys())
+    extra = sorted(pins.keys() - slugs.keys())
+    if missing or extra:
+        raise ValueError(f"declared without gitlink: {missing!r}; gitlink without declaration: {extra!r}")
+    if not slugs:
+        raise ValueError("no submodule members found")
+
+    return [{"path": path, "slug": slug, "sha": pins[path]} for path, slug in slugs.items()]
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    try:
+        print(json.dumps(members()))
+    except ValueError as error:
+        sys.exit(str(error))

title: fix(smoke): hand code-smoke back to root before the root offline step
body:
Follow-through of code#13159 / code#13331 (dezren39/fleet#105).

## What failed

The first publish with #105's new smoke step — run [45193636584](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/45193636584) — built and pushed both images and passed every warm-export leg, then failed the smoke job at exactly one step: **"Warmed shell opens OFFLINE as ROOT, no extra nix flags"**:

```
error: opening Git repository "/__w/fleet/fleet/code-smoke": repository path
'/__w/fleet/fleet/code-smoke' is not owned by current user (libgit2 error code = 7)
```

while fetching the `git+file://` flake input.

## Root cause

The smoke job deliberately runs one tree under two users. The vscode offline step chowns `code-smoke` to **vscode** so vscode's libgit2 fetcher accepts it — and the root acceptance step then ran against that same, now vscode-owned tree. Root's libgit2 applies the same ownership rule in reverse and refuses. The only `safe.directory` root holds in this job covers `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` itself (the pin step), not the `code-smoke` child repo, and `safe.directory` is a fragile fix here anyway: in this job container `$HOME` (`/github/home`) is not root-owned and Nix falls back to the passwd home (`/root`), so which global git config root's fetcher would read is ambiguous.

## Fix

The root step takes the tree back first: `chown -R root:root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/code-smoke"`. Ownership needs no config lookup, and this is the job's last step, so handing the tree back costs nothing. The acceptance shape is untouched — the shell still opens **offline, as root, with no extra nix flags**, and still has to find cargo inside it.

## Are real dispatches exposed to the same trap?

No — checked all three dispatch surfaces:

- **fleet-command**: the composite action's Run-command step runs `git config --global --add safe.directory '*'` as the job user before executing, and the target checkout is made by `actions/checkout` inside the same `--user root` job container, so it is root-owned to begin with.
- **fleet-run**: same shape — checkouts inside the root job container, and its run steps mark `safe.directory '*'` (lines 502/512) before executing.
- **fleet-dispatch-test**: same `safe.directory '*'` guard (line 136).

The trap needs the one ingredient only the smoke job has: a tree deliberately owned by a *different* user than the one opening the shell. The #13159 proof runs passed earlier today precisely because dispatch checkouts and commands share one user.

## Verification

Publish workflow dispatched from this branch; smoke job result reported on the PR once the run completes.

title: fix(executor): bake + prep a working dispatch environment (nixbld, root nix.conf, Rust, bun)
body:
## What this fixes

The remote-dispatch executor environment (developing-today/code#13159, developing-today/code#13331). Every dispatched command runs as **root** in the fleet-build image, where:

1. **Root nix was broken in three stacked ways.** The image's Nix is a single-user install owned by `vscode`; root never reads `~vscode/.config/nix/nix.conf`. A root `nix develop` failed on experimental features, then on the missing `nixbld` group, and the `--option build-users-group ''` workaround ran builds as root and tripped the `/homeless-shelter` purity check.
2. **No Rust toolchain existed.** `cargo: command not found` — the fleet-command cache dirs (`.fleet/cache/{cargo,rustup}`) restore empty on a cold key and nothing installed a toolchain into them.
3. **No bun**, which the repos' TypeScript packages test with.

Every lane bootstrapped around this by hand (rustup into the dispatch caches, the nixbld group recipe, extra nix flags) before any test could run.

**Venue note:** the fixes land here, upstream — developing-today/fleet and developing-today-forks/fleet are actions-only mirrors whose mains converge from this repo (push sync + the daily App pull), and `containers/fleet-build` in this repo is the single source for both published image namespaces (`ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build` and the org mirror `ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build`).

## Changes

- **`containers/fleet-build/Containerfile`** (the durable fix, base image):
  - the `nixbld` group + 32 build users with a **populated member list** (nix rejects a group whose members hold it only as their primary group), using the recipe proven live in this container by the 2026-11-23 9111-02 dispatch (forks/fleet run 45177477297);
  - a system `/etc/nix/nix.conf`: experimental features on, `build-users-group = nixbld`, sandbox off, the fleet substituters/keys. vscode's user config still overrides for vscode (empty build-users-group against the single-user store it owns); everyone else now builds as nixbld users, so the purity check that applies to invoking-user builds does not fire;
  - pinned Rust via rustup (default toolchain **1.99.1**, the fleet-wide `rust-toolchain.toml` pin; per-repo pins still honoured by the shims) and pinned **bun 1.4.5**, both on PATH.
- **`.github/scripts/fleet-executor-prep.sh`** (the runtime half, for images published before the bake): idempotently supplies the same state — nixbld group, system nix.conf, a toolchain installed into the caller's `CARGO_HOME`/`RUSTUP_HOME` (fleet-command's caches, keyed by the target's `rust-toolchain.toml` channel, else 1.99.1), bun — and is a no-op once the baked image is in place. Linux-only; self-skips on macOS.
- **`fleet-command` action**: runs the prep after cache restore, before the command; bun joins the cached paths. (Paths are resolved via `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` — the `github.workspace` expression is the *host* path inside a job container; the first proof run caught exactly that, see below.)
- **`fleet-run.yml`**: checks out the runner repo and runs the prep before the command (its legs had no environment prep at all).
- **`fleet-dispatch-test.yml`**: runs the prep, and its job-level `NIX_CONFIG` now names the real `nixbld` group instead of the empty `build-users-group` that ran builds as root.
- **`fleet-build-container.yml` smoke**: now asserts cargo/rustc/bun as root, the nixbld setup, and a **root, flagless, offline** `nix develop` of the warmed code shell — the #13159 acceptance shape — so the first publish after this merges self-verifies. The image republishes on the workflow's weekly cron or a manual `workflow_dispatch` of `fleet-build-container.yml`; the prep script covers dispatches in the meantime.

## Proof (before → after, all against developing-today/code @ 97764615e)

Before, on the current mirrors (developing-today/fleet, main):

- run [45186834536](https://github.com/developing-today/fleet/actions/runs/45186834536) — `cargo --version && bun --version` → `bash: line 1: cargo: command not found`
- run [45186842535](https://github.com/developing-today/fleet/actions/runs/45186842535) — `cd pkgs/id && nix develop --command cargo test -p id --lib hosted_export` → `error: experimental Nix feature 'nix-command' is disabled`

After, dispatched from this branch (dezren39/fleet @ felix/13159-executor-env):

- **fleet-run** run [45187632834](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/45187632834) — `cargo --version && bun --version && cd pkgs/id && nix develop --command cargo --version` → **success** (prep installed toolchain 1.99.1 + bun 1.4.5 into the image locations; cargo 1.99.1 printed inside the dev shell, as root, no extra nix flags)
- **fleet-command** run [45188409927](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/45188409927) — `cargo --version && bun --version && cd pkgs/fleet && cargo test -p fleet-proxy-proto` → **success** (prep installed the toolchain + bun into the `.fleet/cache` dirs; `test result: ok. 20 passed`)
- **fleet-command, the #13159 acceptance form** run [45188416486](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/45188416486) — `cd pkgs/id && nix develop --command cargo test -p id --lib hosted_export` with no extra flags → **success**

The first after-attempts (runs 45187614820 / 45187622525) failed on a bug in this PR's first cut — the prep step resolved the script via the `github.workspace` expression (host path) instead of `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` — fixed in 0b3e4c5 and re-proven by the runs above.

## Out of scope, recorded on the issue

The `surface=null` queueing half of #13159 is fleet-queue placement capacity, not a workflow defect — finding with evidence posted on code#13159 (comment 7103506745). The Blacksmith auto-placement observation stays with #13146, as already recorded on the issue.

No new dependencies. No schedules created, changed, or retired (the container workflow's existing weekly cron is untouched).

@@ -0,0 +1,189 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# fleet-executor-prep — make a fleet-build job container boring.
+#
+# The dispatch surfaces (fleet-command.yml, fleet-run.yml,
+# fleet-dispatch-test.yml) run arbitrary commands as root inside the
+# fleet-build image. Three environment gaps made every dispatched
+# command improvise its own bootstrap first (developing-today/code
+# #13159, #13331):
+#
+#   1. Root has no nix.conf: the image's Nix is a single-user install
+#      owned by vscode, whose ~/.config/nix/nix.conf root never reads.
+#      As root, `nix develop` therefore failed on experimental
+#      features, then on the missing `nixbld` build-users group, and
+#      the `--option build-users-group ''` workaround ran builds as
+#      root and tripped nix's /homeless-shelter purity check.
+#   2. No Rust toolchain: the image shipped none, and the
+#      fleet-command cache dirs (CARGO_HOME/RUSTUP_HOME under
+#      .fleet/cache) restore empty on a cold key with nothing
+#      installing a toolchain into them.
+#   3. No bun, which the repos' TypeScript packages test with.
+#
+# containers/fleet-build/Containerfile now bakes all three into the
+# image (nixbld group + members, a system /etc/nix/nix.conf, a
+# rustup-managed pinned toolchain, bun). This script is the runtime
+# half for images published before the bake, and a no-op once the
+# baked image is in place: every section checks whether its piece is
+# already present and only installs what is missing. Idempotent.
+#
+# The nixbld recipe is the one proven live in this container by the
+# 2026-11-23 9111-02 dispatch (forks/fleet run 45177477297, recorded
+# on code#13159): the group must exist AND its member list must name
+# the users — nix rejects a group whose members only have it as
+# their primary group ("the build users group 'nixbld' has no
+# members"). With real build users configured, builds run as those
+# users and the /homeless-shelter purity check (which applies to
+# builds running as the invoking user) does not fire; the script
+# deliberately does not touch /homeless-shelter itself, which is the
+# runner machinery's scratch home.
+#
+# Knobs (environment):
+#   FLEET_PREP_SKIP        comma list of sections to skip: nix,rust,bun
+#   RUSTUP_HOME/CARGO_HOME toolchain locations (defaults below)
+#   FLEET_RUST_TOOLCHAIN   default toolchain override
+#   FLEET_TARGET_DIR       target checkout used to discover a
+#                          rust-toolchain.toml channel pin
+#   FLEET_BUN_VERSION      bun pin (default: 1.4.5)
+#   FLEET_BUN_HOME         where bun lands when missing
+#                          (default: /usr/local/bun)
+#
+# Linux only: the macOS fleet-command surface has no container and
+# is out of scope for #13159/#13331, so the script exits 0 there.
+
+set -euo pipefail

+log() { echo "[fleet-executor-prep] $*"; }

+# The nixbld build-users group, with a populated member list (code#13159).
+# Nix's default build-users-group is `nixbld`, but a single-user install
+# never creates it, so any nix invocation by a user without the vscode
+# user's nix.conf (root in GHA job containers) died with "the group
+# 'nixbld' specified in 'build-users-group' does not exist". Nix checks
+# the group's MEMBER LIST — users whose primary group is nixbld but who
+# are not listed are "no members" — so every user is added explicitly.
+# The recipe is the one proven live in this image by the 2026-11-23
+# 9111-02 dispatch (forks/fleet run 45177477297). The runtime half for
+# already-published images is .github/scripts/fleet-executor-prep.sh.

 # Pinned Go, from the official tarball (no nixpkgs, no devcontainer

+# working configuration too (code#13159). Root never reads vscode's
+# ~/.config/nix/nix.conf, so before this file existed a root
+# `nix develop` failed in sequence on experimental features, the
+# missing nixbld group, and — with build-users-group forced empty —
+# builds running as root tripping the /homeless-shelter purity check.
+# vscode's own config still wins for vscode (user config overrides
+# the system file), keeping its build-users-group empty against the
+# single-user store it owns; everyone else builds as the nixbld users
+# created above. Same substituters/keys as the vscode config.
+RUN mkdir -p /etc/nix \
+ && printf '%s\n' \
+      'experimental-features = nix-command flakes ca-derivations' \
+      'build-users-group = nixbld' \
+      'sandbox = false' \
+      'eval-cache = false' \
+      'extra-substituters = https://nix-cache.developing-today.workers.dev https://developing-today.cachix.org' \
+      'extra-trusted-public-keys = nix-cache-1:x/kKZuzyQI3L0/twmOp3w2U68F2ZgM3WnH3ERYKrwf8= developing-today.cachix.org-1:dfIGqIJODUw9V/O9yUrYP2d3tjJtk3SZTDxOBWn9vN4=' \
+      > /etc/nix/nix.conf
+
+# Pinned Rust via rustup, system-wide (code#13331): the runbook's plain
+# `cargo test` form found no toolchain in this image at all. The

+# World-writable: job containers run as root, Codespaces as vscode,

title: docs: document placement dispatch and dispatch-test execution surfaces
body:
## What

`docs/execution-surfaces.md` documented the raw generic runners (`fleet-run` / `org-run`) but not the dispatch route agents actually use. This adds:

- **Placement dispatch** — `fleet queue dispatch` into `fleet-command.yml`: load-based pool selection across the registered surfaces (developing-today org cap 20, dezren39 account cap 40, forks pool for public targets), GitHub-hosted by default, Blacksmith as a budgeted fallback with the paid-minutes override gate, macOS opt-in via `--platform macos`, cache reuse (Actions cache namespace, `--followup` host affinity + artifact reuse, `--push-nix-cache` to the shared R2 Nix cache), and session tracking with portable `OWNER/REPO#RUN_ID` identifiers.
- **Explicit dispatch** — `fleet dispatch-test scan|submit|status` over this repo's fork network with the fleet-dispatch Turso job store.
- **The dispatch-first rule (2026-11-23)** — builds and tests are dispatched, not compiled on agent sandboxes; the laptop is the fallback only for jobs that cannot be dispatched.

Verified live on 2026-11-23: a placement dispatch against developing-today/code was routed to the dezren39/fleet surface because the org pool was saturated (62 active jobs vs cap 20), and completed successfully. The agent runbook lives in developing-today/code (`pkgs/fleet/doc/agents/remote-build-and-test.md`).
head: docs/placement-dispatch-surfaces

files.patch:
@@ -95,6 +95,73 @@ plus the fleet umbrella's public members: `developing-today/zettel`,
 credential available to Actions can read them, so no Actions job may
 pretend to verify them.
 
+### Placement dispatch: `fleet queue dispatch` and `fleet-command`
+
+The generic runners above are the raw workflows. The route agents
+actually use day to day is **placement dispatch** in the `fleet`
+binary (developed in `developing-today/code`, `pkgs/fleet`):
+
+```sh
+fleet queue dispatch --repo <owner/name> --ref <ref> \
+  --command '<cmd>' --dispatch --json
+fleet queue session status <HANDLE>   # async tracking
+fleet queue session result <HANDLE>   # outcome; logs via the run URL
+```
+
+Placement picks a host repo for `.github/workflows/fleet-command.yml`
+from the surface registry (`pkgs/fleet/fleet-surfaces.json` in the
+code repo) by **live load**: it counts active jobs per owner against
+the registered concurrency caps — the developing-today org at 20, the
+dezren39 account at 40 — and sends the job to the least-loaded
+eligible pool. Registered surfaces today are `dezren39/fleet`
+(personal, dispatched as the developing-today GitHub App),
+`developing-today/fleet` (org), and `developing-today-forks/fleet`
+(public targets only), plus a Blacksmith variant of the org surface.
+
+Rules of the road:
+
+- **GitHub-hosted runners are the default.** Blacksmith is a fallback
+  inside a configured free-minute budget; paid Blacksmith minutes
+  require the explicit `--allow-paid-blacksmith <minutes>` override,
+  and `--runner blacksmith` is the only way to pin it.
+- **macOS is opt-in** with `--platform macos` (org macOS concurrency
+  cap 5); Blacksmith is Linux-only.
+- **Caches are keyed for reuse:** the workflow's Actions cache
+  defaults to the `fleet-deps-v1` namespace with branch keys and
+  default-branch restore keys; `--followup <HANDLE|OWNER/REPO#RUN_ID>`
+  keeps a repeat job on the previous run's host and can download its
+  `fleet-output` artifact; `--push-nix-cache` publishes a build's
+  `./result` closure to the shared fleet Nix (R2) cache.
+- Sessions are reconnectable from any seat with the portable
+  `OWNER/REPO#RUN_ID` identifier; the run's log is the Actions log
+  (`gh run view --log`).
+
+`fleet shell --target actions --repo <owner/name> -- <cmd>` is the
+same dispatch through the shell verb (it waits for the result;
+`--detach` returns the session handle instead).
+
+**Dispatch-first rule (2026-11-23):** builds, tests, and other
+CPU-heavy work are dispatched through this route — push the code,
+dispatch against the ref, poll the session, collect the result.
+Compiling on an agent sandbox is the wrong default, and the laptop is
+the fallback only for jobs that cannot be dispatched (NixOS builds
+and activations, stateful or secret-bearing work, a quick
+single-binary check). The agent runbook is
+`pkgs/fleet/doc/agents/remote-build-and-test.md` in
+`developing-today/code`.
+
+### Explicit dispatch: `fleet dispatch-test`
+
+`fleet dispatch-test scan|submit|status` is the older explicit route
+for work inside a fleet-umbrella submodule: `scan` ranks this repo's
+copies (the source plus its fork network) by live Actions load,
+`submit --submodule <name> --ref <ref> --commands '<cmds>'` stores
+the job in the fleet-dispatch Turso store and dispatches
+`fleet-dispatch-test.yml` in the chosen copy, and `status <job-id>`
+reads the stored result. Linux, GitHub-hosted, in the same
+`fleet-build` container. Prefer placement dispatch for general work;
+use this when the job is naturally "run inside submodule X at ref Y".
+
 ### The recurring proof: fleet umbrella verification
 
 `.github/workflows/fleet-umbrella-verify.yml` runs **twice daily**

title: feat(ci): auto-format workflow + treefmt config + format flake app (#89)
body:
## What

Replicates the format auto-fix workflow from the developing-today/code PoC (developing-today/code#2015) into this repo, per #89:

- **`treefmt.toml`** — nixfmt for `*.nix`, shfmt `-i 2` for `*.sh`. The umbrella's own formattable surface is `flake.nix` + `containers/fleet-build/export.sh`; Markdown and workflow YAML are deliberately excluded.
- **`flake.nix`** — additive `apps.<system>.format` output so `nix run .#format -- <files>` runs treefmt from this repo's pinned nixpkgs. `fleetNixpkgsRev` is untouched.
- **`.github/workflows/auto-format.yml`** — the PoC adapted: 15-minute schedule, `cancel-in-progress: false`, `AUTO_FORMAT_LAST_SUCCESS_SHA` guard with 25-hour fallback, 3-attempt push-race retry, `style(treefmt): auto-format on main` bot commits, `GHCR_ORG_PAT` as the automation token (repo-variable writes + bot pushes; the same PAT sync-forks already pushes with), mcpx dogfood block dropped (no dogfood copies here). Formatting never gates a merge — main's branch rules carry only deletion + non-fast-forward protection.
- **`flake.nix` + `containers/fleet-build/export.sh`** — first treefmt pass output, included so the first bot pass is a no-op. The export.sh changes are shfmt's mechanical expansion of semicolon one-liners; semantics unchanged, `bash -n` clean.

## Evidence (worktree off origin/main @ aca908d)

- `nix eval .#fleetNixpkgsRev` → `f9887a8a434bfba06e20dfc77bc8e0628266af84` (unchanged)
- `nix flake show` lists `apps.*.format` on x86_64-linux, aarch64-linux, x86_64-darwin, aarch64-darwin
- Deliberately misformatted scratch `.nix` / `.sh` files corrected by `nix run .#format --` (sh reindented to 2 spaces)
- Second format pass over the repo files: **0 changed** (idempotent)
- `bash -n containers/fleet-build/export.sh` clean

## Merge danger

**Door:** two-way. The flake change is additive (new `apps` output only; consumers read `fleetNixpkgsRev`, verified unchanged). The workflow is schedule-only and self-limiting (formatter output on already-formatted files produces no diff and no commit, so no loop is possible).

**Blast radius:** this repo only. First scheduled pass after merge should exit on the guard or find no changes, since the formatter output is already included here.

Closes #89 pending the post-merge acceptance pass (deliberately misformatted commit on main → correcting bot run), which will be linked on the issue.
head: lane-gu/89-auto-format

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,159 @@
+name: auto-format
+
+# Replicated from the developing-today/code PoC (developing-today/code#2015)
+# per dezren39/fleet#89. CI tier policy: formatting is mechanical and
+# NEVER gates a merge — no treefmt/format context is a required check
+# (main's branch rules carry only deletion + non-fast-forward
+# protection). Instead this workflow runs treefmt on a 15-minute
+# schedule and commits any fixes directly to main as the
+# github-actions bot.
+#
+# Adaptations from the PoC for this repo:
+#   - The umbrella's own formattable surface is flake.nix +
+#     containers/fleet-build/export.sh (see treefmt.toml); the format
+#     entry point is this repo's own flake app: `nix run .#format`.
+#   - The automation token is the existing GHCR_ORG_PAT secret
+#     (classic PAT, repo + workflow scopes — the same token the
+#     sync-forks workflow already pushes with): the default
+#     GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write repository variables (no such key
+#     exists in the workflow permissions vocabulary). The PAT's
+#     pushes trigger downstream checks like a human push.
+#   - The code repo's mcpx dogfood-copy resync block is dropped:
+#     this repo has no dogfood copies.
+#
+# Schedule design (from the PoC — the old push trigger starved under
+# its own concurrency group):
+#   - every 15 minutes, format the files changed since the last
+#     successful pass;
+#   - the repo variable AUTO_FORMAT_LAST_SUCCESS_SHA stores the main
+#     HEAD that pass pushed back (or verified clean); a run whose
+#     HEAD still equals it exits immediately;
+#   - cancel-in-progress is false: a pass is never cancelled, a
+#     queued pass just finds the variable already advanced and exits.
+# The variable is an optimization, not a correctness input: if it is
+# missing, stale, or not an ancestor of HEAD, the run falls back to
+# the last 25 hours of changed files, and a failed variable update
+# only means the next run re-checks the same range. Loops cannot
+# occur: a bot commit contains only formatter output, and formatting
+# already-formatted files produces no diff and no commit.
+
+on:
+  schedule:
+    - cron: "*/15 * * * *"
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: write
+
+# One format pass at a time on main; a pass is never cancelled
+# mid-commit.
+concurrency:
+  group: auto-format-main
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+jobs:
+  treefmt:
+    name: treefmt auto-format
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          token: ${{ secrets.GHCR_ORG_PAT }}
+          fetch-depth: 0

+      - uses: DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action@3138316df39ed29be04236d7ffc686fa525866aa # v23

+        env:
+          LAST_SUCCESS_SHA: ${{ vars.AUTO_FORMAT_LAST_SUCCESS_SHA }}
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GHCR_ORG_PAT }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          # Record a successful pass: store the main HEAD this run
+          # pushed back (or verified clean) so the next run can skip
+          # or diff against it. Best-effort by design (see header).
+          record_success() {
+            local sha
+            sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
+            if gh api -X PATCH "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/variables/AUTO_FORMAT_LAST_SUCCESS_SHA" -f value="$sha" 2>/dev/null; then
+              echo "Recorded AUTO_FORMAT_LAST_SUCCESS_SHA=$sha"
+            elif gh api -X POST "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/variables" -f name="AUTO_FORMAT_LAST_SUCCESS_SHA" -f value="$sha" 2>/dev/null; then
+              echo "Created AUTO_FORMAT_LAST_SUCCESS_SHA=$sha"
+            else
+              echo "::warning::could not update AUTO_FORMAT_LAST_SUCCESS_SHA; the next run will re-check this range."
+            fi
+          }
+          changed_file="$(mktemp)"
+          trap 'rm -f "$changed_file"' EXIT
+          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
+          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
+          max_attempts=3
+          for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= max_attempts; attempt++)); do
+            # A formatter commit is based on the checkout's main. Always
+            # start from the latest remote tip so a push race can retry the
+            # formatting pass rather than rebasing stale formatter output.
+            git fetch origin main
+            git reset --hard origin/main
+            head_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
+            if [[ -n "${LAST_SUCCESS_SHA:-}" && "$LAST_SUCCESS_SHA" == "$head_sha" ]]; then
+              echo "main is unchanged since the last successful format pass ($head_sha); nothing to do."
+              exit 0
+            fi
+            : > "$changed_file"
+            if [[ -n "${LAST_SUCCESS_SHA:-}" ]] \
+               && git cat-file -e "${LAST_SUCCESS_SHA}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null \
+               && git merge-base --is-ancestor "$LAST_SUCCESS_SHA" HEAD; then
+              git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR "$LAST_SUCCESS_SHA...$head_sha" > "$changed_file"
+            else
+              git log --since="25 hours ago" --pretty=format: --name-only \
+                | sort -u | while IFS= read -r f; do
+                    if [[ -n "$f" && -f "$f" ]]; then
+                      printf '%s\n' "$f"
+                    fi
+                  done > "$changed_file"
+            fi
+            mapfile -t changed_files < "$changed_file"
+            if ((${#changed_files[@]} == 0)); then
+              echo "No changed files to format."
+              record_success
+              exit 0
+            fi
+            # treefmt.toml covers only *.nix and *.sh, so the write
+            # pass can never touch workflow files; nothing is excluded.
+            format_files=("${changed_files[@]}")
+            printf 'Formatting %s file(s):\n' "${#format_files[@]}"
+            printf '  %s\n' "${format_files[@]}"
+

title: fix(sync-upstream): scope the daily pull to the two App-mirror forks (#87)
body:
## What

Scopes the `sync-upstream` daily pull to the two forks where its authentication can actually work — `developing-today/fleet` and `developing-today-forks/fleet` — and says why, in the workflow header and in `docs/execution-surfaces.md`.

## Why (#87)

The old guard was `github.repository != 'dezren39/fleet'`, so the job attempted to run on **every** fork. On the ~100 new org forks it can never authenticate: it mints a token for the developing.today app (5454422), which is installed only on the developing.today orgs, and the org-level `FLEET_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` there belongs to the fleet app (5612056) — a JWT for one app signed with the other app's key is rejected. Since #93/#94 those forks are kept current by the central `sync-forks` push (PAT + merge-upstream on every push to main; first fully clean run 102/102), so the local pull is pure failure surface there. On the two mirror forks the pull is the working mechanism (repo-level key matches, rulesets bypass only that app; latest runs 2026-11-22 all success) and stays untouched.

Deliberately **not** re-pointing to the fleet app (5612056): it is also not installed on the new orgs, and the mirrors' rulesets bypass only the developing.today app — that change would break the working backstop without fixing the new forks.

## Measured move

Forks where a `sync-upstream` run can be attempted-and-fail: **~102 → 0**. The job remains live exactly on the 2 forks where it passes.

## Test

`.github/workflows/sync-upstream.test.sh` (new) pins the guard, the app-id/key pairing, and the header scope note. Verified: passes on this branch; fails (rc 1) when the guard is reverted to the old form; `shellcheck` clean; workflow YAML parses (`yq`).

Refs #87 (stays open for the app-install track, code#6645).

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Regression test for the sync-upstream scope guard (dezren39/fleet#87).
+#
+# The daily pull mints a developing.today app (5454422) token from the
+# FLEET_APP_PRIVATE_KEY secret. That pairing can only authenticate in
+# the two App-mirror forks (developing-today/fleet and
+# developing-today-forks/fleet): the app is installed only on the
+# developing.today orgs, those repos hold the matching repo-level key,
+# and their branch rulesets bypass only that app. Every other fork is
+# kept current by the central sync-forks push instead, so the job must
+# stay guarded to exactly those two repositories — an upstream-only
+# guard re-arms a daily job that can only fail on ~100 forks.
+set -euo pipefail
+cd "$(dirname "$0")"
+f=sync-upstream.yml
+
+fail() { echo "FAIL: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+grep -Fq "if: github.repository == 'developing-today/fleet' || github.repository == 'developing-today-forks/fleet'" "$f" \
+  || fail "job guard must scope the pull to the two App-mirror forks (#87)"
+
+if grep -Fq "github.repository != 'dezren39/fleet'" "$f"; then
+  fail "old upstream-only guard is back: the pull would run on forks where it cannot authenticate (#87)"
+fi

+grep -Fq "app-id: 5454422" "$f" \

+
+grep -Fq "secrets.FLEET_APP_PRIVATE_KEY" "$f" \

+
+grep -Fq "SCOPE (#87)" "$f" \
+  || fail "the header must keep the #87 scope note explaining the guard"
+
+echo "ok: sync-upstream is scoped to the two App-mirror forks (#87)"

title: fleet-build variant: :full cache export mode=max -> mode=min (#88)
body:
Fixes the deterministic `build`-leg failure of the gated fleet-build variant (#88).

**Root cause** (diagnosis recorded on #88 by Lane EI, verified in runs 45072661780 / 45099045788): the `Build :full` step fails at `#18 exporting cache to registry` with `error writing layer blob: denied: permission_denied: The token provided does not match expected scopes.`

The `full` Containerfile target is `FROM base`, so `cache-to ...,mode=max` re-exports the base stage's layers too. Those blobs already exist in GHCR under the **developing-today**-owned `fleet-build` package (the same job's "Push :base" step publishes them there), so buildx attempts a cross-repository blob mount into `ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:buildcache-full` — and GHCR denies the mount because the dezren39 classic PAT has no access to the developing-today package. The `:base` export succeeds with `mode=max` because its layers mount from public upstream images, not from a GHCR package.

**Change** (one line + comment): the `:full` `cache-to` in `fleet-build-variant.yml` goes from `mode=max` to `mode=min`. mode=min exports only the final stage's own layers — for `full` that is the nar-cache import layer, the one layer that changes per pin — so no cross-repository mount is attempted. The `:base` cache is untouched.

**Test:** the acceptance test for this leg is the gated variant run itself — the leg's bot records green/red on #88 per run. YAML re-parsed after the edit; the effective `cache-to` for the `Build :full` step reads `type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:buildcache-full,mode=min`. This PR does not touch the workflow's triggers, so the verification run is the next gated variant run on main after merge; #88 stays open until the bot records the leg green.

**Not in this slice:** the same `mode=max` pattern exists on the `:full` step of `fleet-build-container.yml` (the publish workflow, which logs in as `github.actor`); left untouched here — noted on #88 for its owner.
