@@ -218,7 +218,16 @@ jobs:
             ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full
             ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full-sha-${{ github.sha }}
           cache-from: type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:buildcache-full
-          cache-to: type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:buildcache-full,mode=max
+          # mode=min, NOT mode=max (#88): the full target is FROM base, so
+          # mode=max also re-exports the base stage's layers. Those blobs
+          # already live in the developing-today-owned fleet-build package
+          # (pushed by the "Push :base" step below), and GHCR denies the
+          # cross-repository blob mount for the dezren39 cache token
+          # ("token provided does not match expected scopes"), failing the
+          # whole build leg at "exporting cache to registry". mode=min
+          # exports only the full stage's own layers (the nar-cache import
+          # layer), which is the layer that actually changes per pin.

title: fleet: converge org runner cache workflow

Bring the existing developing-today/fleet runner and cache behavior into the canonical upstream workflow so the action-only mirror can sync cleanly.

- Preserve optional public-repo anonymous checkout when GHCR_ORG_PAT is absent; make GHCR_ORG_PAT optional for reusable calls.

title: Add dispatch-only Fleet command runner
body:
Adds the generic `fleet-command.yml` dispatch/reusable workflow and its composite action.

- Run a command against a target checkout on GitHub-hosted Linux, Blacksmith Linux, or explicitly requested macOS.
- Restore default Rust/Go dependency and build caches, support additional cache paths and fallback prefixes, and upload `fleet-output` artifacts for followups.
- Keep this workflow limited to manual/reusable dispatch; it does not gate PRs or main.

Validation: YAML parsing, `actionlint`, and `git diff --check`. This runner branch is intended to merge alongside the developing-today/code dispatcher change.

title: sync-forks: push main out to every fork on update
body:
## What

New workflow `sync-forks.yml` (Drew, 2026-11-22): when dezren39/fleet `main` updates, push that main out to **every fork** immediately, instead of waiting for each fork's daily pull.

- **Trigger:** push to `main` here, plus `workflow_dispatch`. A job-level guard (`github.repository == 'dezren39/fleet'`) makes the file inert in the forks that receive it through their sync — the same guard pattern `sync-upstream.yml` uses in mirror image.
- **Sync call:** `POST /repos/<fork>/merge-upstream` with `branch: main` — fast-forward when the fork is a strict prefix, clean merge otherwise; never a force-push, never an auto-resolved conflict. Fork-local deltas (e.g. developing-today/fleet's fleet-run deltas) survive a clean merge.
- **Auth:** the classic PAT in this repo's existing `GHCR_ORG_PAT` secret (the workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot write other repos). A missing secret fails the run immediately, before any fork is touched.
- **Fork census at filing time:** 102 forks, none archived (archived forks would be skipped, not failed).
- **Failure contract:** every fork is attempted no matter how many fail. The job fails only at the end, with the failed forks and the API's reasons in the log and job summary, and **one issue filed in developing-today/code** carrying the same list as a todo.
- **Relationship to `sync-upstream.yml`:** unchanged. The App-driven daily pull stays as the backstop — and as the only route for ruleset-locked fork mains whose sole bypass is the developing.today App (developing-today/fleet, developing-today-forks/fleet). If those forks refuse a PAT sync, their refusal lands on this run's failure list, which is the signal to extend their bypass or accept the daily cadence for them.

## Verification

- YAML parses; the fork enumeration half of the script (paginated forks API + archived filter) was run live from the sandbox: 102 forks, 0 archived.
- The `merge-upstream` call shape was proven live on `dpope3/fleet`: "Successfully fetched and fast-forwarded from upstream dezren39:main."
- First full run: `workflow_dispatch` immediately after merge; its summary (and the code-repo issue, if any forks fail) is the end-to-end evidence.
head: archer/sync-forks-workflow

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,152 @@
+name: sync-forks (push main out to every fork)
+
+# Fixes land HERE, on dezren39/fleet main, and the forks follow
+# (Drew, 2026-11-22). The forks already pull from upstream once a
+# day (sync-upstream.yml, App-driven, defined in this tree); this
+# workflow is the push-driven complement: every push to main here
+# immediately offers the new main to EVERY fork, so the fleet
+# converges in minutes instead of at the next daily pull. The daily
+# pull stays as the backstop for anything this run misses.
+#
+# How a fork is synced: GitHub's merge-upstream API
+# (POST /repos/<fork>/merge-upstream, branch main) — the same call
+# a human makes with the "Sync fork" button. It fast-forwards a
+# fork that is a strict prefix of upstream and clean-merges
+# otherwise; it never force-pushes and never auto-resolves a
+# conflict. Fork-local deltas (e.g. developing-today/fleet's
+# fleet-run fork deltas) survive a clean merge; a true divergence
+# conflicts and lands on the failure list below.
+#
+# Auth: the classic PAT in this repo's GHCR_ORG_PAT secret. The
+# workflow's own GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write other repositories, and
+# dispatching requires write access here, which is the gate. Known
+# caveat: fork mains locked by a ruleset whose only bypass is the
+# developing.today App (developing-today/fleet,
+# developing-today-forks/fleet) may refuse a PAT sync — those forks
+# keep converging through their App-driven daily pull, and their
+# refusal shows up on this run's failure list, which is the signal
+# to extend their bypass or accept the daily cadence for them.
+#
+# Failure contract (Drew, 2026-11-22): attempt EVERY fork, no
+# matter how many fail. The job fails only at the END, with the
+# failed forks listed in the log and the job summary, and one
+# issue filed in developing-today/code carrying the same list as
+# a todo. Archived forks are skipped, not failed (they are
+# read-only by definition). A missing PAT is a configuration
+# error and fails the run immediately, before any fork is touched.
+#
+# This file only ever acts in dezren39/fleet itself (the job-level
+# guard below): the forks receive this file through their sync,
+# and it must be inert there.
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  sync:
+    name: push main to all forks
+    if: github.repository == 'dezren39/fleet'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 120
+    steps:
+      - name: Sync every fork from dezren39/fleet@main
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GHCR_ORG_PAT }}
+          UPSTREAM: dezren39/fleet
+          BRANCH: main
+          TODO_REPO: developing-today/code
+        run: |
+          set -uo pipefail
+
+          if [ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
+            echo "::error::GHCR_ORG_PAT secret is not set on $UPSTREAM; no fork was touched."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+
+          work="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/sync-forks"
+          mkdir -p "$work"
+          synced="$work/synced.txt"; current="$work/current.txt"
+          failed="$work/failed.txt"; skipped="$work/skipped.txt"
+          : > "$synced"; : > "$current"; : > "$failed"; : > "$skipped"
+
+          # Every fork, every page. Archived forks are recorded as
+          # skipped up front so the loop only sees syncable ones.
+          gh api --paginate "repos/$UPSTREAM/forks?per_page=100" \
+            --jq '.[] | select(.archived == true) | .full_name' > "$skipped" || true
+          mapfile -t forks < <(gh api --paginate "repos/$UPSTREAM/forks?per_page=100" \
+            --jq '.[] | select(.archived == false) | .full_name')
+
+          echo "Syncing ${#forks[@]} forks from $UPSTREAM@$BRANCH (skipped archived: $(wc -l < "$skipped"))"
+
+          for fork in "${forks[@]}"; do
+            if out=$(gh api -X POST "repos/$fork/merge-upstream" -f branch="$BRANCH" 2>&1); then
+              mtype=$(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.merge_type // "unknown"' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
+              if [ "$mtype" = "none" ]; then
+                echo "$fork" >> "$current"
+                echo "CURRENT  $fork"
+              else
+                echo "$fork ($mtype)" >> "$synced"
+                echo "SYNCED   $fork ($mtype)"
+              fi
+            else
+              msg=$(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.message // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
+              [ -n "$msg" ] || msg=$(printf '%s' "$out" | head -c 300)
+              echo "$fork — $msg" >> "$failed"
+              echo "FAILED   $fork — $msg"
+            fi
+          done
+
+          n_synced=$(wc -l < "$synced"); n_current=$(wc -l < "$current")
+          n_failed=$(wc -l < "$failed"); n_skipped=$(wc -l < "$skipped")
+
+          {
+            echo "## Fork sync from $UPSTREAM@$BRANCH"
+            echo ""
+            echo "- Synced: $n_synced"
+            echo "- Already current: $n_current"
+            echo "- Skipped (archived): $n_skipped"
+            echo "- Failed: $n_failed"
+            if [ "$n_failed" -gt 0 ]; then
+              echo ""
+              echo "### Failed forks"
+              echo ""
+              sed 's/^/- /' "$failed"
+            fi
+          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+
+          if [ "$n_failed" -eq 0 ]; then
+            echo "All forks synced or current."
+            exit 0
+          fi
+
+          # One todo issue in the code repo carrying the failure
+          # list. If filing itself fails, the job still fails with
+          # the list in the summary and log above.
+          body="$work/issue-body.md"
+          {
+            echo "The sync-forks workflow in dezren39/fleet pushed \`$BRANCH\`"
+            echo "(commit $GITHUB_SHA) out to every fork. The forks below could"
+            echo "not be synced and need a human/agent pass — most likely a"
+            echo "merge conflict with fork-local deltas, or a ruleset that"
+            echo "refuses a PAT sync (the App-driven daily pull in"
+            echo "

title: fleet-run: carry dispatch_id in run display title (code#8371)
body:
## What

Part of developing-today/code#8371 (fleet-place exact run correlation):

- Adds an optional `dispatch_id` input to `fleet-run.yml` in both the `workflow_dispatch` and `workflow_call` forms (string, default blank — manual dispatches and existing callers are unchanged).
- Adds top-level `run-name: "fleet-run ${{ inputs.dispatch_id }}"` so the runs list API returns the id in the run's `display_title`.

## Why

fleet-place (`placement.rs` in developing-today/code) correlates a dispatch to its Actions run by snapshot exclusion, which cannot prove apart two dispatches landing in the same poll window (Codex P1 residual on developing-today/code PR #8325). With this change, fleet-place generates a unique id per dispatch, passes it as the `dispatch_id` input, and matches the run whose display title carries that id — exact correlation. The matching code change lands in developing-today/code alongside the same treatment for `org-run.yml`; this PR merges first so the input exists before fleet-place starts sending it.

title: fleet-run: either-or runner input (github | blacksmith)
body:
## What

`fleet-run.yml` gains either-or runner selection, per Drew's order (2026-11-06) that a fleet job must be able to run on GitHub-hosted **or** Blacksmith runners — not Blacksmith-only. This is the canonical repo, so the change propagates to the org forks through the existing sync arrangement; no org copy is touched.

## Inputs (mirrored in `workflow_dispatch` and `workflow_call`)

| input | applies to | dispatch type | `workflow_call` type | default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `runner` | run legs | choice `github`\|`blacksmith` | string | `github` |
| `setup_runner` | setup job | choice `github`\|`blacksmith` | string | `github` |

Mapping (same labels as the precedent): `blacksmith` → `blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404`, anything else → `ubuntu-24.04`, via the same `inputs.X == 'blacksmith' && 'blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404' || 'ubuntu-24.04'` expression org-run uses.

## Precedent and one deliberate difference

Names, labels, and expression shape mirror `org-run.yml` in developing-today/code: the legs' `runner` input from PR #5417, `setup_runner` from PR #6639. Difference: org-run defaults `setup_runner` to `blacksmith`; fleet-run defaults **both** inputs to `github`, because this repo is a personal repo and Blacksmith is orgs-only — it cannot run here at all, so the default must work everywhere. Org forks where the Blacksmith app is installed can pass `blacksmith` explicitly. (`workflow_call` inputs are plain strings because workflow_call has no choice type; the mapping treats any non-`blacksmith` value as GitHub-hosted.)

## Compatibility

- Unchanged: allowlist validation, jobs-JSON matrix expansion, timeouts, permissions, triggers (dispatch + reusable call only — no new triggers).
- Callers passing neither input see no change: `fleet-umbrella-verify.yml` (the in-repo reusable caller) keeps running entirely on `ubuntu-24.04`.
- Container caveat: none found. Blacksmith runners are drop-in Ubuntu 24.04 runners, and the legs' container spec (`ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full`, `--user root`) is provider-agnostic — GitHub runs job containers on Blacksmith runners the same way. No leg step assumes GitHub-hosted hardware. A Blacksmith proof dispatch is nevertheless impossible on this personal repo (Blacksmith is orgs-only); the blacksmith path can only be exercised from an org fork.

## Sibling-workflow runner report (report only — no changes made)

- `fleet-build.yml`: does not exist in this repo.
- `fleet-build-container.yml`: hardcodes `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` in all 4 jobs, no runner input.
- `fleet-build-variant.yml`: hardcodes `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` in all 5 jobs, no runner input.

Both siblings publish/build the fleet images rather than running dispatched fleet jobs, so they are out of scope here; giving them the same treatment would be a separate, identically-shaped change if wanted.

## Verification

- YAML validated (Python `yaml.safe_load`): both trigger forms carry both inputs; setup/legs `runs-on` resolve to the mapping expressions; container, permissions untouched.
- Proof dispatch on this repo with the default (github) runner, command `true` against `dezren39/fleet`: see the run link in the merge comment / PR discussion once run.

title: ci: generic fleet-dispatch-test workflow (code#6580 phase 2)
body:
Phase 2 of developing-today/code#6580. The generic `fleet dispatch-test` workflow lives in this repo only; copies (source + fork network) inherit it as execution homes.

- `workflow_dispatch` only, sole input `job_id` (no triggers — code#5663 ruling stands).
- Payload from the Turso jobs store: **submodule + ref + commands** — checks out this repo, checks out the named submodule at the named ref, runs the commands inside it.
- Runs in `ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full` (this repo's partial preloaded nix cache; same wiring as fleet-run.yml; NIX_CONFIG mirrors export.sh for root steps).
- Always writes status/exit/output-tail back to the store; output log uploaded as an artifact (default return path).
head: fleet-dispatch-test-workflow

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,198 @@
+name: fleet-dispatch-test
+
+# Generic explicit-dispatch job runner for `fleet dispatch-test`
+# (design: developing-today/code#6580, phase 2 — Drew's corrected
+# execution model). This workflow lives ONLY in the fleet repo
+# (dezren39/fleet, the submodule umbrella); the repo's copies —
+# the source plus every fork found by following its fork network —
+# inherit it, and those copies are the execution homes that
+# `fleet dispatch-test scan` discovers and selects between.
+#
+# workflow_dispatch ONLY — no push/PR/schedule triggers, per the
+# standing no-auto-CI ruling (code#5663, closed: no triggers).
+#
+# The job payload lives in the fleet-dispatch-jobs Turso store
+# under the internal job id passed as the sole input. The payload
+# names a SUBMODULE of this repo + a REF + COMMANDS: this workflow
+# checks out the fleet repo, checks out the named submodule at
+# the named ref, runs the commands inside the submodule checkout,
+# and ALWAYS writes status/output back to the store, even on
+# failure (a cancelled run is the best-effort exception — its row
+# stays `running`, which `status` reports honestly).
+#
+# Nix cache: the job runs in ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full,
+# the image whose baked Nix store is this repo's partial preloaded
+# cache — per-submodule dev-shell closures realised from each
+# submodule's flake.lock exactly as committed (see
+# containers/fleet-build/warm-manifest.txt and
+# fleet-build-container.yml) — with the fleet substituters baked
+# in. This is the same image and cache wiring fleet-run.yml uses;
+# nothing new is invented here. NIX_CONFIG below mirrors
+# containers/fleet-build/export.sh because job-container steps run
+# as root, which has no nix.conf of its own.
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      job_id:
+        description: "fleet dispatch-test job id"
+        required: true
+        type: string
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  run-job:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 120
+    container:
+      image: ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full
+      options: --user root
+    env:
+      TURSO_URL: ${{ vars.DISPATCH_TURSO_URL }}
+      TURSO_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DISPATCH_TURSO_TOKEN }}
+      JOB_ID: ${{ inputs.job_id }}
+      NIX_CONFIG: |
+        experimental-features = nix-command flakes ca-derivations
+        sandbox = false
+        eval-cache = false
+        build-users-group =
+        extra-substituters = https://nix-cache.developing-today.workers.dev https://developing-today.cachix.org
+        extra-trusted-public-keys = nix-cache-1:x/kKZuzyQI3L0/twmOp3w2U68F2ZgM3WnH3ERYKrwf8= developing-today.cachix.org-1:dfIGqIJODUw9V/O9yUrYP2d3tjJtk3SZTDxOBWn9vN4=
+    steps:
+      - name: Nix profile on PATH
+        shell: bash
+        run: echo "/home/vscode/.nix-profile/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
+
+      - name: Fetch job by id and mark running
+        id: fetch
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          if [ -z "${TURSO_URL}" ] || [ -z "${TURSO_TOKEN}" ]; then
+            echo "dispatch store not configured (DISPATCH_TURSO_URL var / DISPATCH_TURSO_TOKEN secret missing)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          jq -n \
+            --arg id "$JOB_ID" --arg rid "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" \
+            --arg url "$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID" \
+            '{requests: [
+              {type: "execute", stmt: {sql: "select submodule, target_ref, coalesce(commands, script) from jobs where id = ?", args: [{type: "text", value: $id}]}},
+              {type: "execute", stmt: {sql: "update jobs set status = '"'"'running'"'"', run_id = ?, run_url = ?, updated_at = strftime('"'"'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'"'"', '"'"'now'"'"') where id = ?", args: [{type: "integer", value: $rid}, {type: "text", value: $url}, {type: "text", value: $id}]}},
+              {type: "close"}
+            ]}' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/pipeline.json"
+          curl -sS -X POST "$TURSO_URL/v2/pipeline" \
+            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TURSO_TOKEN" \
+            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+            --data @"$RUNNER_TEMP/pipeline.json" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/resp.json"
+          if ! jq -e '.results[0].type == "ok"' "$RUNNER_TEMP/resp.json" > /dev/null; then
+            echo "dispatch store fetch failed for job $JOB_ID:"
+            head -c 1000 "$RUNNER_TEMP/resp.json"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          row=$(jq -c '.results[0].response.result.rows[0] // empty' "$RUNNER_TEMP/resp.json")
+          if [ -z "$row" ]; then
+            echo "job $JOB_ID not found in dispatch store"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          submodule=$(jq -r '.results[0].response.result.rows[0][0].value // ""' "$RUNNER_TEMP/resp.json")
+          ref=$(jq -r '.results[0].response.result.rows[0][1].value // ""' "$RUNNER_TEMP/resp.json")
+          jq -r '.results[0].response.result.rows[0][2].value // ""' "$RUNNER_TEMP/resp.json" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/job-commands.sh"
+          if [ -z "$submodule" ]; then
+            echo "job $JOB_ID names no submodule (pre-phase-2 row?) — nothing to run"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "submodule=$submodule" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          echo "ref=$ref" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

title: docs(execution-surfaces): document the fork mirror regime
body:
Adds the closing section to `docs/execution-surfaces.md` recording the regime put in place today: the org forks are actions-only mirrors of this repo — the daily `sync-upstream` pull (defined here so it is part of the synced tree), the app-token route it takes and why (repo rulesets cannot bypass the GitHub Actions integration; org rulesets are Team-gated; the workflow token cannot push workflow-file payloads), and the lockdown rulesets on both forks' `main` (creation/update/deletion restricted, force pushes blocked, sole bypass the developing.today app). This repo stays unlocked.

This merge is also the post-lockdown payload: both forks' next sync dispatches must pull it in with a real push through their rulesets.
head: docs/fork-mirror-regime

files.patch:
@@ -149,3 +149,36 @@ Posture:
 | Long-running services (pm-stack, opencode, OpenChamber) | Laptop | Supervision and state live here |
 | Exploratory / interactive sessions | Codespace (or the laptop's opencode) | A driver sits in it; disposable |
 | Anything needing tailnet/LAN or SOPS-rendered secrets | Laptop | Only the laptop holds those keys and routes |
+
+## The forks are mirrors: daily sync + actions-only lockdown
+
+`dezren39/fleet` (this repo) is the only fleet repo of the three that
+takes commits. `developing-today/fleet` and
+`developing-today-forks/fleet` are mirrors — **actions only**:
+
+- **Daily pull.** `.github/workflows/sync-upstream.yml` is defined
+  here, upstream, so it is part of the tree the forks sync (a
+  fork-local file would be erased by its own sync). It runs daily
+  (04:23 UTC) and on dispatch, and in a fork pulls this repo's `main`
+  in: fast-forward when the fork is a strict prefix, a clean merge
+  otherwise. A content conflict aborts the merge, fails the run
+  loudly, and files an issue here **as the developing.today app** —
+  it never force-pushes and never auto-resolves a conflict. In this
+  repo the job is a guarded no-op.
+- **The sync runs as the app.** GitHub's ruleset model cannot name
+  the GitHub Actions integration as a bypass actor on a repository
+  ruleset (it is not part of the owner org), and organization
+  rulesets are Team-plan gated. So the sync mints a developing.today
+  app installation token (`actions/create-github-app-token`; key in
+  the `FLEET_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secret on the fork repos) and checks
+  out / pushes with it. The app token is also what lets a payload
+  that touches workflow files land: the plain workflow token is
+  refused at push for those, and there is no `workflows` key in the
+  `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions schema.
+- **Lockdown.** Each fork's `main` carries an active branch ruleset
+  ("main: actions-only (commits happen upstream)") restricting
+  creation, update, and deletion and blocking force pushes for
+  everyone, with a single bypass: the developing.today app. The
+  app lands the forks' own rare direct changes (placement registry,
+  convergences) by PR; everything else arrives via the daily pull.
+  This repo, the upstream, is deliberately **not** locked.

title: fix(sync-upstream): drop the invalid workflows: job permission
body: #82 added `workflows: write` to the job `permissions:` — there is no such key in the GITHUB_TOKEN permissions schema, and with it the workflow file fails to parse (both forks' dispatches 422'd: `Unexpected value 'workflows'`). The workflow token cannot push workflow-file payloads regardless of the permissions block; that gate is precisely why the sync pushes with the app token, which carries the app's own Workflows permission. This restores `contents: write` alone and documents why.

title: feat: sync-upstream — daily pull from dezren39/fleet for the org forks
body:
Adds `.github/workflows/sync-upstream.yml`: a daily (04:23 UTC) + dispatchable job that pulls this repo's `main` into the org forks (`developing-today/fleet`, `developing-today-forks/fleet`).

Design points:
- Defined **upstream** so it is part of the tree the forks sync — a fork-local copy would be erased by its own sync.
- Fast-forward when the fork is a strict prefix of upstream; clean merge otherwise; a merge conflict aborts, pushes nothing, and fails loudly (plus a best-effort issue filed here — the workflow token is fork-scoped, so the loud failure is the guaranteed signal).
- Never force-pushes. Guarded no-op in dezren39/fleet itself.

This is the flow-down half of the org forks' actions-only lockdown: commits happen upstream and arrive there by this pull.
head: feat/sync-upstream

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,85 @@
+name: sync-upstream (daily pull from dezren39/fleet)
+
+# The org forks of this repo (developing-today/fleet and
+# developing-today-forks/fleet) are ACTIONS-ONLY mirrors: nobody commits
+# there — commits happen here, upstream, and flow down. This workflow is
+# therefore defined HERE, upstream, so it is part of the tree the forks
+# sync; a fork-local workflow file would be erased by the very sync it
+# performs.
+#
+# In a fork, the daily run pulls dezren39/fleet main into the fork's
+# main: fast-forward when the fork is a strict prefix of upstream, a
+# clean merge otherwise. A merge CONFLICT (true content divergence)
+# aborts the merge and fails the job loudly — it never force-pushes and
+# never auto-resolves a conflict. In dezren39/fleet itself the job is a
+# guarded no-op.
+#
+# On conflict the job also tries to open an issue on dezren39/fleet.
+# The in-workflow token is scoped to the fork repo only, so that filing
+# is best-effort (expected to fail without an app token); the loud job
+# failure is the guaranteed signal.
+
+on:
+  schedule:
+    - cron: "23 4 * * *"
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: write
+
+concurrency:
+  group: sync-upstream
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+jobs:
+  sync:
+    name: pull upstream main
+    if: github.repository != 'dezren39/fleet'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    steps:
+      - name: Check out this fork's main
+        uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+
+      - name: Pull dezren39/fleet main
+        id: pull
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
+          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
+          git remote add upstream https://github.com/dezren39/fleet.git
+          git fetch upstream main
+          local_head=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
+          up_head=$(git rev-parse upstream/main)
+          echo "fork head:     $local_head"
+          echo "upstream head: $up_head"
+          if [ "$local_head" = "$up_head" ]; then
+            echo "already up to date with dezren39/fleet main — nothing to pull"
+            echo "result=up-to-date" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          if git merge-base --is-ancestor "$local_head" "$up_head"; then
+            git merge --ff-only "$up_head"
+            echo "result=fast-forward" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          else
+            if ! git merge --no-edit "$up_head"; then
+              git merge --abort || true
+              echo "::error title=sync-upstream divergence::dezren39/fleet main conflicts with this fork's main — merge aborted, nothing pushed. Commits belong in dezren39/fleet."
+              echo "result=conflict" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+              exit 1
+            fi
+            echo "result=merged" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          fi
+          git push origin HEAD:main
+          echo "synced: $local_head -> $(git rev-parse HEAD)"
+
+      - name: File an issue upstream on conflict (best effort)
+        if: failure() && steps.pull.outputs.result == 'conflict'
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+        run: |
+          gh issue create --repo dezren39/fleet \
+            --title "sync-upstream: ${{ github.repository }} main has diverged from upstream" \
+            --body "The daily sync-upstream run in ${{ github.repository }} hit a merge conflict pulling dezren39/fleet main, aborted the merge, and pushed nothing. Run: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}. Commits belong upstream in dezren39/fleet; this fork's main needs a manual convergence." \
+          || echo "::warning::could not file the upstream issue with the workflow token (expected without an app token) — the failed job above is the signal."

Live authorship census (default-branch + per-branch commit scans, PR authorship, divergence vs parent) of all 38 remaining repos: **zero transfers** — every repo carries dezren39-authored work (31 REAL forks, fleet + zig-overlay internal, the 4 §9 working forks), reproducing the original census exactly. `nixos-unattended-installer` stays HELD: pure by all measures but still a live flake input of developing-today/code. Final counts: forks 38, vendored 70; no backup store ports needed (no transfers).
head: forks-reconciliation-record

files.patch:
@@ -2,8 +2,7 @@
 
 Status: **EXECUTED 2026-11-04** — Drew approved execution of the §3
 real-fork move at 07:02 CST ("yes do it all"); the §8 archive move was
-executed earlier the same day. Executed records: §8 (archive) and §9
-(real forks) at the end of this document. Companion docs: `docs/execution-surfaces.md`
+executed earlier the same day. Executed records: §8 (archive), §9 (real forks) and §10 (reconciliation sweep) at the end of this document. Companion docs: `docs/execution-surfaces.md`
 (surface routing), `docs/placement.md` in the fleet copies (surface
 registry).
 
@@ -367,3 +366,60 @@ Branch counts moved between the morning census and the move-day
 snapshots (openchamber 104 → 52, opencode 96 → 57) through the
 repos' own branch-cleanup workflows — each transfer was verified
 against a fresh same-hour snapshot, not the census.
+
+## 10. Reconciliation sweep — EXECUTED 2026-11-04 (later pass)
+
+The forks-org sweep agent's session ended before its census record
+was written down anywhere durable; this pass re-derived the
+classification of every repo still in developing-today-forks from
+live evidence, to confirm nothing pure was left behind and nothing
+real was at risk.
+
+- Method: for all 38 repos — default-branch commit counts filtered
+  by author (`dezren39`, `developing-today[bot]`), divergence vs
+  parent (compare ahead/behind), PR authorship, and — for every
+  repo whose default branch carried none of Drew's commits — a
+  per-branch authorship scan (the §8 `helper` lesson: divergence
+  can live entirely on side branches).
+- Result: **zero transfers.** Every remaining repo carries
+  dezren39-authored work:
+  - The four §9 working forks: opencode (1531 default-branch
+    commits by dezren39), openchamber (1303), kaneo (3),
+    nix-openclaw (4).
+  - Fleet-internal: `fleet` (70) and `zig-overlay` (its parent is
+    dezren39/zig-overlay).
+  - 22 forks with dezren39 commits on the default branch —
+    incl. nixpkgs (1 commit, 3 PRs, 264 ahead of NixOS/nixpkgs),
+    home-manager, charm, emanote, koanf (plus 3 in-repo PRs),
+    nixpkgs-vim-extra-plugins (52), scoop-charmbracelet (20).
+    microvm.nix, server.nix and sops-nix in this set are also
+    live flake inputs of developing-today/code (flake.lock
+    nodes, re-verified this pass).
+  - 8 forks whose only dezren39 work is a small patch branch:
+    amp (`time`, 1 commit), runiq (`time`, 1), raytrace.roc
+    (`update`, 1), libsql-client-go (`antlr4-dep`, 1), porkbun
+    (`improvements`, 3), sqlite-antlr4-parser (`antlr4-dep`, 3),
+    ssh (`conpty`, 2), octto-fork (`feat/nix-dev-shell` +
+    `feat/top-level-model`, 3).
+  - `log`: no dezren39 commits on the default branch, but open
+    PR #1 authored by dezren39 with its head branch in-repo —
+    a working fork.
+  This reproduces the original census exactly (31 REAL + fleet +
+  zig-overlay + the held repo below = the 34 post-sweep
+  remainder, plus the 4 §9 arrivals = 38), so the 54 §8
+  transfers stand as the complete pure set.
+- HELD (unchanged from §8): `nixos-unattended-installer` is pure
+  by every authorship/divergence measure — identical to parent
+  chrillefkr/nixos-unattended-installer, single branch, zero
+  dezren39/app commits or PRs — but it remains a live flake
+  input of developing-today/code (flake.nix
+  `unattended-installer.url =
+  "github:developing-today-forks/nixos-unattended-installer"`
+  plus a flake.lock node, re-verified this pass). It moves only
+  together with a repoint of that input; left in forks pending
+  that decision.
+- Final counts: developing-today-forks 38 repos,
+  developing-today-vendored 70. Backup stores: no transfers
+  this pass, so no store ports — the forks-org mirrors under
+  `~/backups/github/developing-today-forks/` already cover the
+  remaining repos (36 stores, incl. opencode/openchamber/kaneo).

title: fix(smoke): pin code checkout to committed submodule rev; develop on a writable copy (fleet#70)
body:
Refs #70.

The smoke job checked out developing-today/code at floating main and ran `nix develop .#fleet --offline` in the root-owned checkout as vscode. When code's flake.nix inputs drift from its committed flake.lock (the fork reorganization did exactly this), nix tries to refresh the lock mid-smoke and dies writing it: `Permission denied`. An offline smoke should never need that write - and a floating checkout can also drift past the closure that was actually warmed.

Both candidate fixes from #70, combined:
1. Pin the smoke checkout to this repo's committed `code` submodule pin - the exact rev the warm-export legs realised, whose lock is the nar-cache key basis - resolved live from the fleet checkout at runtime, so the smoke always tests what was warmed.
2. Run the develop against a vscode-owned copy of the checkout, so a lock refresh (should one ever be attempted) lands in the copy instead of dying on the root-owned tree. The copy is runner-local; the offline guarantee is unchanged.

Proof run to follow on this issue after merge.
head: fix/70-smoke-code-pin

files.patch:
@@ -255,9 +255,30 @@ jobs:
           # 41513747440); runuser from root does not, and HOME must be
           # pointed at the vscode home for its Nix profile to resolve.
           runuser -u vscode -- env HOME=/home/vscode bash -lc 'nix --version && go version'
+      # fleet#70: smoke the code rev the warm-export legs actually
+      # realised — this repo's committed `code` submodule pin — not
+      # code's floating main. A floating checkout can carry a
+      # flake.nix whose inputs have moved past its committed lock
+      # (the fork reorganization did exactly this), and then
+      # `nix develop --offline` tries to refresh the lock mid-smoke:
+      # a write the offline test should never need, against a closure
+      # that was never warmed. The pin's lock is the nar-cache key
+      # basis, so the pinned rev is the one whose shell is guaranteed
+      # to be in the image's store.
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          submodules: false
+      - name: Resolve the committed code submodule pin
+        id: code-pin
+        run: |
+          pin=$(git ls-tree HEAD code | awk '{print $3}')
+          if [ -z "$pin" ]; then echo "ERROR: no code submodule pin at HEAD" >&2; exit 1; fi
+          echo "code submodule pin: $pin"
+          echo "pin=$pin" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           repository: developing-today/code
+          ref: ${{ steps.code-pin.outputs.pin }}
           path: code-check
       - name: Warmed shell opens OFFLINE from the image's store
         run: |
@@ -266,6 +287,15 @@ jobs:
           # hit the same wall (run 41523275400) — mark paths safe in
           # vscode's git config first.
           runuser -u vscode -- env HOME=/home/vscode git config --global --add safe.directory '*'
+          # The smoke reads the checkout but must never need to write
+          # it: run the develop against a vscode-owned copy, so a lock
+          # refresh (should one ever be attempted) lands in the copy
+          # instead of dying on the root-owned tree (fleet#70). The
+          # copy is runner-local disk only — the offline guarantee is
+          # unchanged: the shell still has to come from the image's
+          # store.
+          cp -a "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/code-check" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/code-smoke"
+          chown -R vscode:vscode "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/code-smoke"
           # code warms its lean `fleet` shell (see warm-manifest.txt),
           # not the default shell — open the one that was warmed.
-          timeout 600 runuser -u vscode -- env HOME=/home/vscode bash -lc 'cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/code-check" && nix develop .#fleet --offline --accept-flake-config --command true'
+          timeout 600 runuser -u vscode -- env HOME=/home/vscode bash -lc 'cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/code-smoke" && nix develop .#fleet --offline --accept-flake-config --command true'

title: ci: remove push trigger from fleet-build-container (no PR/commit jobs)
body:
Drew's ruling (2026-11-04): **no PR or commit jobs** — CI runs via schedule, `workflow_dispatch`, `workflow_call` and the placement surfaces only. This extends the trigger removal already landed in developing-today/code (#5501), developing-today-forks/opencode (#1635) and developing-today-forks/openchamber (#1584).

Change (workflow `on:` block only — machine-verified: everything outside `on:` is byte-identical, kept triggers unchanged):

- `fleet-build-container.yml` — `push` removed; weekly schedule + `workflow_dispatch` (with the `fresh_build` input) kept.

Already clean, untouched: `fleet-build-variant.yml` (schedule + dispatch), `fleet-run.yml` (dispatch + `workflow_call`), `fleet-umbrella-verify.yml` (schedule + dispatch).
head: ci/no-push-pr-triggers

files.patch:
@@ -26,11 +26,6 @@ name: fleet-build container
 # `fresh_build` ignores the Docker layer cache AND the nar cache.
 
 on:
-  push:
-    branches: [main]
-    paths:
-      - "containers/fleet-build/**"
-      - ".github/workflows/fleet-build-container.yml"
   schedule:
     - cron: "0 6 * * 1"
   workflow_dispatch:

body: Appends the section 9 executed record for the real-fork migration to docs/fork-migration-plan.md and flips the document status from plan-only to executed. All four forks are transferred and verified at developing-today-forks; the record includes the repoint PR list, the section 6 findings (same-admin transfers carried secrets, webhooks and workflow disable states), and the open items (G2 app install, automation PAT scope, hatch-personal cron definitions).
head: fork-migration-executed

files.patch:
@@ -1,7 +1,9 @@
 # Fork migration plan — developing-today → developing-today-forks (+ pure-clone archive move)
 
-Status: **plan only** (prepared 2026-11-04). No repo moves until Drew rules
-execution timing per repo. Companion docs: `docs/execution-surfaces.md`
+Status: **EXECUTED 2026-11-04** — Drew approved execution of the §3
+real-fork move at 07:02 CST ("yes do it all"); the §8 archive move was
+executed earlier the same day. Executed records: §8 (archive) and §9
+(real forks) at the end of this document. Companion docs: `docs/execution-surfaces.md`
 (surface routing), `docs/placement.md` in the fleet copies (surface
 registry).
 
@@ -283,3 +285,84 @@ string plus parsed flake.lock nodes (owner == developing-today).
   fork now occupies developing-today-vendored/iffy, which is
   the collision blocking the singular org's TruemarkDev/iffy
   (recorded above, awaiting a ruling).
+
+
+## 9. Real-fork move — EXECUTED 2026-11-04
+
+All four §3 repos were transferred from `developing-today` to
+`developing-today-forks` with the user-token transfer API, in plan
+order (nix-openclaw, kaneo, openchamber, opencode), each verified at
+the destination against a same-day snapshot: default-branch head SHA
+identical, branch/issue/PR counts carried, fork parent intact, and
+the old `developing-today/<repo>` path answering with a redirect.
+
+- **nix-openclaw**: head `b4f1c9d0`, 14 branches, 0 issues/PRs. §6
+  re-check at move time: no Actions secrets, no webhooks, no deploy
+  keys — nothing to re-provision. No fleet references existed.
+- **kaneo**: head `1e7cb2d8`, 42 branches, 4 open PRs. No secrets or
+  webhooks. Repoint (app PR, merged): developing-today/code #5454
+  (aggregator program.ts, board fixture, repo-universe.yaml).
+- **openchamber**: head `709ce4b0` (includes its own repoint PR),
+  52 branches, 41 issues, 6 PRs. Repoints (app PRs, merged):
+  openchamber #1580 (its own opencode flake pin — merged *before* the
+  transfer, see deviations), developing-today/code #5463,
+  dezren39/nix #1466, dezren39/fleet #65 (.gitmodules). Pinned rev
+  `794e5f5c` verified fetchable at the new home.
+- **opencode**: head `ce1aec22`, 57 branches, 71 issues, 12 PRs.
+  Repoints (app PRs, merged): developing-today/code #5465,
+  dezren39/nix #1468, dezren39/fleet #66 (.gitmodules). All pinned
+  revs (`4175c630`, `ae5d5920`, `2d912e02`) verified fetchable at the
+  new home; openchamber's lock pin resolves against the moved repo.
+
+§6 findings that update the checklist's assumptions: for transfers
+where the same admin controls both orgs, GitHub **carried the repo
+Actions secrets and webhooks with the repo** — verified by name lists
+and unchanged `updated_at` timestamps at the destination
+(openchamber's 5 secrets, opencode's `REPO_AUTOMATION_TOKEN`, the
+supabase CI webhook on both). Manually-disabled workflow states also
+carried (opencode 15, openchamber 4 — the push-workflow posture is
+unchanged). No manual secret re-provisioning was needed. There were
+no org-level Actions secrets in developing-today and no environment
+secrets in either repo, so the many upstream-inherited workflow
+secret references (Apple/iOS signing, NPM, Discord, …) had nothing
+provisioned to carry — they were unprovisioned before the move and
+remain so.
+
+Two deliberate side effects in the repoint PRs: dispatch's
+`APP_INSTALLED_REPOS` (developing-today/code) no longer lists
+opencode/openchamber — the developing.today app is **not installed
+on developing-today-forks** (verified with the fleet-paperwork
+helper: no installation for that owner), so both repos are app-dark
+until grants item G2 lands; the entries return then.
+`pm-stack/kaneo-projects.json` still records openchamber's pre-move
+installation id; it resolves with the same G2 install.
+
+Open items after the move:
+
+- **G2** (Drew, needs GitHub sudo): install the developing.today app
+  on developing-today-forks with access to the moved repos.
+- The `REPO_AUTOMATION_TOKEN` value carried, but the fine-grained
+  PAT behind it (`developing-today-code-automation`) is scoped to
+  developing-today repos; Drew needs to extend/re-approve it for
+  developing-today-forks before automation that spends it there
+  works.
+- Muse surfaces: hatch-personal cron definitions and repo-health
+  goal workspaces still name `developing-today/opencode` (the plan's
+  §4 item). Redirects bridge git/API access; the app has no write
+  access to hatch-personal, so the definition repoint rides that
+  repo's own maintenance flow.
+- Codespaces repository grants naming the moved repos: re-check per
+  the standing devcontainer-grants question.
+
+Deviations from the plan as written: (1) openchamber's own opencode
+repoint merged before openchamber's transfer rather than inside the
+opencode window (§3 cascade order) — the app cannot write in the
+forks org, so pre-transfer was the only app-authenticated slot; the
+dangling-pin window was minutes and no fleet build consumes
+openchamber's own lock standalone. (2) The §5 pm-dispatch lane pause
+was not invoked; windows were kept to minutes and transfers are
+atomic, with redirects bridging in-flight git/API traffic. (3)
+Branch counts moved between the morning census and the move-day
+snapshots (openchamber 104 → 52, opencode 96 → 57) through the
+repos' own branch-cleanup workflows — each transfer was verified
+against a fresh same-hour snapshot, not the census.

title: fleet-build: an optional leg's hard death no longer blocks the publish (#28)
body:
Implements the approved fix for #28 (ruling: Drew, 2026-11-04 — "yes do it all").

**Problem.** In `fleet-build-container.yml`, `build-full` has `needs: warm-export` (the whole matrix). The graceful optional-leg path works (export step is `continue-on-error`), but a HARD job death of an optional leg (nix in run 41564555311 — runner/container killed mid-step) fails the `warm-export` job, and default needs semantics then skip `build-full` and `smoke` — even though all three required repos (code, opencode, openchamber) exported fine.

**Fix.**
- `build-full`: `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` — the publish runs on any non-cancelled needs outcome. The real gate is unchanged and stays inside the job: the merge step hard-fails if a REQUIRED repo's nar cache is missing or empty. A cancelled run still blocks the publish.
- `smoke`: `if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.build-full.result == 'success' }}` — the transitive half of the #28 proposal, tightened so smoke never runs against a stale image after a build-full failure.

**Note on file choice.** #28's jobs (build-full/smoke, optional legs per `containers/fleet-build/warm-manifest.txt`) live in the plain pipeline, `fleet-build-container.yml` — not the gated variant, whose legs are strict by design and whose build requires every leg. The variant is untouched.

One file, +13 lines (two `if:` lines plus explanatory comments). YAML validated.
head: fix-optional-leg-gating

files.patch:
@@ -176,6 +176,14 @@ jobs:
 
   build-full:
     needs: warm-export
+    # fleet#28: an optional leg's HARD job death (runner killed mid-step)
+    # fails its warm-export job, and default needs semantics would skip
+    # this publish even though every required repo exported fine.
+    # !cancelled() runs the publish on any non-cancelled needs outcome;
+    # the merge step below stays the real gate — it hard-fails if a
+    # REQUIRED repo's nar cache is missing or empty. A cancelled run
+    # still blocks the publish.
+    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
     runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
     timeout-minutes: 30
     steps:
@@ -230,6 +238,11 @@ jobs:
     # the exact way consuming repos will use it, including a warmed
     # shell opening with the network off.
     needs: build-full
+    # fleet#28 (transitive): smoke whenever build-full actually
+    # succeeded, regardless of what happened to the optional export
+    # legs upstream of it — and never against a stale image after a
+    # build-full failure.
+    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.build-full.result == 'success' }}
     runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
     timeout-minutes: 30

title: docs: fork migration plan
body: Migration plan for moving the real forks (opencode, openchamber, kaneo, nix-openclaw) from developing-today to developing-today-forks: transfer mechanics, redirect limits, per-repo reference inventories (flake inputs/locks, umbrella gitlinks, pm-stack config), sequencing with freeze windows, the non-transferring items checklist, rollback, and the parameterized pure-clone archive-move checklist. Plan only - no moves executed. The developing-today-forks/fleet stand-up landed alongside this (fork of dezren39/fleet, verified in sync at creation).
head: fork-migration-plan

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,225 @@
+# Fork migration plan — developing-today → developing-today-forks (+ pure-clone archive move)
+
+Status: **plan only** (prepared 2026-11-04). No repo moves until Drew rules
+execution timing per repo. Companion docs: `docs/execution-surfaces.md`
+(surface routing), `docs/placement.md` in the fleet copies (surface
+registry).
+
+## 0. Facts on the ground (verified 2026-11-04)
+
+- Source org: `developing-today` (free plan). Forks org:
+  `developing-today-forks` (87 repos, 83 of them forks; Drew is admin).
+- Fleet copies already stood up: `developing-today/fleet` (fork of
+  `dezren39/fleet`, 2026-11-04) and `developing-today-forks/fleet`
+  (same parent, 2026-11-04, head == upstream head at creation).
+- The **developing-today GitHub App is NOT installed on
+  developing-today-forks** — that org's installations are `claude` and
+  `developing-today-backup` only. Installing the app there (with access
+  to each moved repo) is grants-batch item #1 and a precondition for any
+  app-driven write in the forks org.
+- Fork-network shape of the moving repos (parents, from the API):
+  - `developing-today/opencode` ← parent `dezren39/opencode`
+  - `developing-today/openchamber` ← parent `dezren39/openchamber`
+  - `developing-today/kaneo` ← parent `usekaneo/kaneo`
+  - `developing-today/nix-openclaw` ← parent `openclaw/nix-openclaw`
+  The first two are two-level chains (upstream → personal fork → org
+  fork). A transfer keeps the repo inside its fork network; default PR
+  targeting follows the new owner.
+
+## 1. Classification state
+
+- Planned as REAL forks (this plan): opencode, openchamber, kaneo,
+  nix-openclaw — **subject to census confirmation**. The census
+  (divergence: ahead/behind vs upstream, unique branches, our open
+  PRs) classifies all 15 developing-today forks; if it reclassifies
+  one of these four as pure, it drops to the §8 list; if it finds
+  another real fork, that repo joins §3 sequencing by reference count.
+- `developing-today/fleet` is excluded: it is the placement copy, not a
+  migration subject.
+
+## 2. Transfer mechanics (every move, both directions of §8 too)
+
+Per repo:
+
+- [ ] Snapshot: default-branch head sha, open issue/PR counts, Actions
+      secret NAMES (values are write-only), webhook URLs, app
+      installations, branch-protection/settings summary, deploy keys
+      and outside collaborators if any.
+- [ ] Announce + start the write-freeze window (§5).
+- [ ] Transfer as repo admin (user token — the app has no
+      administration permission):
+      `POST /repos/developing-today/<repo>/transfer` with
+      `{"new_owner": "developing-today-forks"}`. When the same admin
+      controls both orgs no acceptance step should be needed; if a
+      transfer lands pending, accept it from the forks-org side.
+- [ ] Verify: repo resolves under the new owner, default-branch sha
+      identical to the snapshot, issues/PRs/branches/tags/releases
+      intact (transfer carries all of them).
+- [ ] **Hold the old name.** Do not create any repo named `<repo>`
+      under developing-today afterwards (see redirect limits).
+
+Redirect behavior and its limits:
+
+- Web and git URLs (`github.com/developing-today/<repo>`, clone /
+  fetch / push over https and ssh) redirect to the new location
+  indefinitely **while the old name stays unclaimed**.
+- Most REST endpoints answer with a redirect to the canonical URL;
+  clients should still be repointed (§4) — the redirect is a bridge,
+  not the end state.
+- **Limit:** creating a new repo at `developing-today/<same name>`
+  permanently kills the redirect — the old URL then serves the new
+  repo. Any future fresh fork at the old address is a deliberate,
+  announced cut, never a side effect.
+- Nix `github:` fetchers in flake.lock pin owner/repo + rev and fetch
+  through the redirect during the gap. Same rule: bridge only; the
+  repoint + relock in §4 ships inside the move window.
+
+## 3. Sequencing (least-referenced first, one repo per window)
+
+1. **nix-openclaw** — zero load-bearing references found (no flake
+   inputs, no pm-stack hits; only historical hatch-personal scratch
+   logs). Moves first as the transfer dress rehearsal.
+2. **kaneo** — references live in the pm-stack aggregator (§4). The
+   kaneo *service* repair (code#5398, aggregator sign-in 500) lands
+   first; the repo move must not be conflated with that breakage.
+3. **openchamber** — flake inputs in nix + code, umbrella gitlink,
+   pm-stack projector/dispatch config. Its §4 repoint set is staged
+   before the window opens.
+4. **opencode** — most referenced (flake inputs in nix, code, *and*
+   openchamber; umbrella gitlink; dispatch config; daily repo-health
+   writes). Moves last, shortest freeze, repoints pre-staged.
+
+Cascade rule (mcpx → opencode → openchamber → nix): moving opencode
+changes openchamber's pinned input URL; nix pins both repos. Repoint
+PRs are prepared in advance and merge inside the same window in
+consumer order — openchamber's lock repoint first, then code's, then
+nix's — each proven by a lock fetch/resolve check before the next
+lands. Redirects bridge any skew inside the window; nothing waits on
+the next cascade round.
+
+## 4. Reference inventory (measured 2026-11-04)
+
+Counts are file/node hits for the literal `developing-today/<repo>`
+string plus parsed flake.lock nodes (owner == developing-today).
+
+### opencode
+
+- `dezren39/nix`: flake.nix input (1); flake.lock node `opencode`
+  rev `2d912e02fce3`. Prose/skill refs in the same repoint PR:
+  systemPackages.nix, configuration.nix, justfile, ARCHITECTURE.md,
+  docs/services.md, planning/README.md, .agents/skills/*.
+- `developing-today/code`: flake.nix input (1); flake.lock nodes
+  `opencode` rev `4175c630bf83` and `opencode_2` rev `ae5d592093e8`.
+  pm-stack: `pm-stack/dispatch/src/config.ts`,
+  `pm-stack/dispatch/src/github.ts` (live dispatch config),
+  `pm-stack/projector/` (README, .env.example),
+  `pm-s

title: docs: execution surfaces — where fleet work runs
body:
Adds `docs/execution-surfaces.md`: the fleet's execution-surface design (Drew, 2026-11-04).

Work is divvied by state and supervision, not by repo:

- **Laptop** — stateful, secret-bearing, live: deploys and home-manager activations, the long-running services (pm-stack, opencode, OpenChamber), primary clones, and anything needing tailnet/LAN or SOPS-rendered secrets.
- **GitHub Actions** — stateless, reproducible, parallel: CI and clean-room build proofs, scheduled health checks, container builds, and ad-hoc cross-repo jobs through the generic runners (`fleet-run` here for personal/fleet scope, `org-run` in developing-today/code for org scope — same repo+command job schema against an allowlist).
- **Codespaces** — interactive/overflow seats a human or agent drives live: anywhere access and disposable per-branch work. Never daemons, never scheduled jobs; posture ≤3 live, delete-on-merge, ~15 min idle timeout, bounded by the Pro core-hour budget (180/month).

The doc carries the per-job-class routing table, both runners' schemas and `fleet-run`'s allowlist (the five core repos plus the umbrella's public members; the private members are deliberately excluded), the twice-daily fleet umbrella verification that proves the split, and the laptop-only list. The companion implementation (fleet-run `workflow_call` + the verification caller) is in #57.
head: execution-surfaces-doc

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,151 @@
+# Execution surfaces — where fleet work runs
+
+The fleet has three places work can execute: the **laptop**, **GitHub
+Actions**, and **Codespaces**. Work is divvied between them by *state
+and supervision*, not by which repo it touches:
+
+- If it holds state, needs a rendered secret, or supervises something
+  live, it runs on the **laptop**.
+- If it is stateless, reproducible, and parallel, it runs in **GitHub
+  Actions**.
+- If a human or an agent needs to sit inside it and drive it live, it
+  runs in a **Codespace**.
+
+Every recurring job in the fleet names its surface when it is created.
+When a job seems to belong nowhere, that is a design smell — surface it,
+don't quietly run it wherever is convenient.
+
+## The laptop (amd-6) — stateful, secret-bearing, live
+
+The laptop is the fleet's machine of record. It owns:
+
+- **Deploys and activations** — home-manager generations and every
+  switch; a deploy is a laptop act, verified from the laptop.
+- **Long-running services** — the pm-stack (dispatch, aggregator,
+  git-sync), the opencode server, OpenChamber, the mcpx daemon, Kaneo
+  and the rest of the pm stack. Services are supervised here, nowhere
+  else.
+- **Primary clones** — `~/git/*` primaries are deploy sources; work
+  happens in worktrees, and a primary's dirt is never discarded by a
+  bystander.
+- **Secrets in use** — anything needing SOPS/Bitwarden-rendered
+  credentials, and anything that must reach the tailnet or the LAN.
+
+Nothing scheduled or stateful may move off the laptop without changing
+this document first.
+
+## GitHub Actions — stateless, reproducible, parallel
+
+All fleet repos are public, so hosted runners are free and unlimited.
+Actions owns:
+
+- **Clean-room build proofs** — a build that must not be able to see
+  the laptop's state (dirty trees, warm caches, staged work) runs here.
+- **Scheduled health checks** — cron-driven verification that is pure
+  function of a commit (see the umbrella verification below).
+- **Container builds** — the `fleet-build` image pipeline
+  (`fleet-build-variant.yml`, every 30 min) publishes
+  `ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build` and advances the umbrella pins.
+- **Ad-hoc cross-repo jobs** — through the generic dispatch runners
+  below.
+
+Push-triggered workflows in `developing-today/code`,
+`developing-today/opencode`, and `developing-today/openchamber` stay
+**disabled** (Drew, 2026-11-02); Actions work there is dispatched,
+scheduled, or called — never push-triggered.
+
+### The generic runners
+
+Two reusable runners take *repo + command* jobs against an allowlist,
+so an agent or a human never re-implements checkout + validation:
+
+| | `fleet-run` | `org-run` |
+|---|---|---|
+| Home | `dezren39/fleet`, `.github/workflows/fleet-run.yml` | `developing-today/code` |
+| Scope | personal / fleet repos | developing-today org repos |
+| Triggers | `workflow_dispatch`, `workflow_call` | `workflow_dispatch`, `workflow_call` |
+
+Both share one job model. The `jobs` input is a JSON array of entries
+in three shapes:
+
+- **Fan-out** — `{"command": "…", "repos": [{"repo", "ref?", "depth?"}]}`:
+  one leg per repo, the same command in each.
+- **Together** — `{"command": "…", "together": [{…}, …]}` (≥2 repos):
+  exactly one leg; the repos are cloned side-by-side under
+  `repos/<basename>` and the command runs once from the workspace
+  root, for cross-repo work.
+- **Flat** — `{"repo", "ref?", "depth?", "command"}`: exactly one leg.
+
+`ref` is a branch, tag, or SHA (blank = the repo's default branch).
+`depth` is the fetch depth (absent = 1, 0 = full history — the escape
+hatch for bisection/archaeology). Legs run in parallel with fail-fast
+off, each in the published `ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full`
+image, each capped by `timeout_minutes` (5–120, default 60), and the
+expanded matrix is capped at 32 legs. `fleet-run` additionally offers a
+single-shot dispatch form (`repo` choice + `ref` + `command`).
+
+`fleet-run`'s allowlist is the five core fleet repos —
+`developing-today/code`, `developing-today/opencode`,
+`developing-today/openchamber`, `dezren39/nix`, `dezren39/fleet` —
+plus the fleet umbrella's public members: `developing-today/zettel`,
+`developing-today/.github`, `developing-today/zulip-archive`,
+`developing-today/hardware-doc`, `dezren39/zettel`,
+`dezren39/hatch`. The umbrella's private members (`dezren39/cairn`,
+`dezren39/hatch-personal`) are deliberately **not** on it: no
+credential available to Actions can read them, so no Actions job may
+pretend to verify them.
+
+### The recurring proof: fleet umbrella verification
+
+`.github/workflows/fleet-umbrella-verify.yml` runs **twice daily**
+(06:23 and 18:23 UTC) and on dispatch. It is the standing proof that
+the split above works:
+
+1. **plan** reads the umbrella's submodule pins off the run's commit.
+2. **verify** calls `fleet-run` once per public member, pinned at
+   exactly that SHA, shallow: each leg checks the member out and
+   asserts `HEAD` equals the recorded pin — the pin resolves, fetches,
+   and is current. The private members are verified as *recorded*
+   (a full 40-hex pin exists in the tree) and reported as
+   recorded-only; if umbrella membership ever drifts from the
+   workflow's lists, the plan job fails loudly instead of silently
+   dropping a member.
+3. **smoke** pulls `ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full` and
+   runs the fleet's own container smoke — the same command the
+   variant pipeline gates on — so the published image's defining
+   tools (go, git, jq, nix) are proven present.
+
+## Codespaces — interactive and overflow seats
+
+Codespaces are seats, not servers. They are for:
+
+- **Anywhere access** — a full environment from a browser or phone.
+- **Disposable per-branch work** — clean-room PR/sweep verification on
+  a branch, deleted when the branch merges.
+- **Overflow seats** — a live session while the laptop is asleep or
+  busy (knowing idle-stop w

title: fleet-run: reusable form + twice-daily umbrella verification
body:
Implements the fleet side of the execution-surfaces split (design: docs PR, `docs/execution-surfaces.md`):

**`fleet-run.yml`**
- Gains a `workflow_call` trigger whose inputs mirror the dispatch inputs (single-shot `repo`/`ref`/`command`, `jobs`, `timeout_minutes`); the caller passes `GHCR_ORG_PAT` explicitly, since the checkout PAT is not ambient for a called workflow. Dispatch behaviour is unchanged — the setup job's synthesis/validation paths were re-run locally against single-shot, legacy fan-out, and the new umbrella jobs payloads, plus a negative case (`dezren39/cairn` is rejected: *"repo dezren39/cairn is not on the fleet-run allowlist"*).
- The jobs-form allowlist grows from the five core fleet repos to also cover the fleet umbrella's **public** members (`developing-today/zettel`, `developing-today/.github`, `developing-today/zulip-archive`, `developing-today/hardware-doc`, `dezren39/zettel`, `dezren39/hatch`). The private members (`dezren39/cairn`, `dezren39/hatch-personal`) stay off it: no credential available to Actions can read them. Member visibility was verified with two independent `gh api` calls after an early tool preview misreported two repos.

**`fleet-umbrella-verify.yml`** (new) — twice daily (06:23 / 18:23 UTC) + dispatch:
- `plan` reads the umbrella's submodule pins off the run's commit and emits one fleet-run leg per public member, pinned at exactly that SHA; private members are verified as recorded (full pin present) and a coverage assertion fails the job loudly if umbrella membership ever drifts from the workflow's lists.
- `verify` calls `fleet-run` with those legs; each leg checks the member out shallow at the pin and asserts `HEAD` == pin.
- `smoke` pulls `ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full` and runs the fleet's own container smoke (the same command `fleet-build-variant` gates on: `go version && git --version && jq --version && nix --version`).

Local pre-flight: both files parse; the plan script and fleet-run's setup script were executed against the real tree — 10 fetch-verified legs + 2 recorded-only, matrix expansion green. A dispatched proof run follows the merge.
head: fleet-run-callable

files.patch:
@@ -51,23 +51,35 @@ name: fleet-run (generic dispatch runner)
 # the escape hatch for the rare history work (bisection,
 # archaeology); everything else wants the shallow default. The
 # setup job validates the expanded legs before
-# anything runs: every repo must be one of the five fleet repos,
+# anything runs: every repo must be on the allowlist (the five
+# core fleet repos plus the fleet umbrella's public members),
 # and the total leg count is capped at 32. Serial composition
 # needs no machinery of its own — it is just shell: put
 # `cmd1 && cmd2` (or `cmd1; cmd2`) in one command string.
 #
 # Guardrails, such as they are, are structural: the workflow only
 # runs on workflow_dispatch (dispatching requires write access to
-# this repo), the target repos are restricted to the five fleet
-# repos (the choice input in single-shot form, an allowlist in the
-# setup job for the jobs form), each leg's timeout is capped at
+# this repo) or as a reusable workflow from a caller in this repo,
+# the target repos are restricted to an allowlist (the five core
+# fleet repos in the single-shot choice input; the jobs-form
+# allowlist in the setup job additionally covers the fleet
+# umbrella's public members so the scheduled umbrella verification
+# can pin-check every public member repo), each leg's timeout is
+# capped at
 # 120 minutes, and every command runs verbatim with its full log on
 # the run page — nothing is hidden or cached away. There is
 # deliberately no concurrency group: every leg gets a fresh runner
 # and container, legs share nothing mutable (the hosted nix caches
 # are content-addressed and append-only), so parallel runs are safe
 # and a group would only serialise them.
 #
+# The same setup/run jobs are also exposed as a reusable workflow
+# (workflow_call, inputs mirroring the dispatch ones) so scheduled
+# fleet jobs can run through this runner instead of re-implementing
+# checkout and validation — the caller in this repo is

+# behaviour is unchanged.
+#

@@ -0,0 +1,136 @@
+name: fleet umbrella verification
+
+# Twice-daily verification of the fleet umbrella, run through the
+# generic runner (fleet-run.yml, called in its reusable form):
+#
+#   plan   — read this repo's submodule pins off the commit being
+#            run, and turn every public member into one fleet-run
+#            leg pinned at exactly that SHA.
+#   verify — fleet-run checks each member out at its pinned SHA
+#            (shallow) and asserts HEAD == the pin: the pin
+#            resolves, it fetches, and it is the commit the
+#            umbrella records.
+#   smoke  — pull ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full and run
+#            the fleet's own container smoke (the same command the
+#            variant pipeline gates on): the defining toolchain
+#            (go, git, jq, nix) answers inside the published image.
+#
+# The umbrella's private members (dezren39/cairn,
+# dezren39/hatch-personal) cannot be fetched from GitHub Actions:
+# no credential available to this repo can read them — the same
+# posture as the umbrella's own best-effort private init. The plan
+# job verifies their pins are recorded and reports them as
+# recorded-only; every other member is fetch-verified. If the
+# umbrella gains or loses a member, the plan job fails loudly
+# until this file's RECORDED_ONLY list is reconciled — a member is
+# never silently dropped from verification.
+#
+# Why this exists: docs/execution-surfaces.md. Scheduled health
+# checks are GitHub Actions work, and this is the recurring job
+# that proves the split (and fleet-run's reusable form) end to end.
+
+on:
+  schedule:
+    - cron: "23 6,18 * * *"
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+defaults:
+  run:
+    shell: bash
+
+jobs:
+  plan:
+    name: plan
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    outputs:
+      jobs: ${{ steps.pins.outputs.jobs }}
+    steps:
+      - name: Check out the umbrella at the run's commit
+        uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 1
+      - name: Turn the submodule pins into fleet-run legs
+        id: pins
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+
+          # Members GitHub Actions cannot fetch (private, and no
+          # credential in this repo can read them). Their pins are
+          # verified as recorded; see the header comment.
+          recorded_only='["dezren39/cairn", "dezren39/hatch-personal"]'
+
+          # path -> slug from .gitmodules, path -> sha from the tree.
+          subs=$(git config -f .gitmodules --get-regexp 'submodule\..*\.url' | while read -r key url; do
+            name=${key#submodule.}; name=${name%.url}
+            path=$(git config -f .gitmodules --get "submodule.$name.path")
+            slug=${url#https://github.com/}; slug=${slug%.git}
+            jq -cn --arg path "$path" --arg slug "$slug" '{path: $path, slug: $slug}'
+          done | jq -s '.')
+
+          pins=$(git ls-tree HEAD | awk '$2 == "commit" {print $3, $4}' | while read -r sha path; do
+            jq -cn --arg path "$path" --arg sha "$sha" '{path: $path, sha: $sha}'
+          done | jq -s '.')
+
+          members=$(jq -c -n --argjson subs "$subs" --argjson pins "$pins" '
+            [$subs[] | . + {sha: (.path as $p | $pins[] | select(.path == $p) | .sha)}]')
+
+          count=$(jq 'length' <<<"$members")
+          [ "$count" -ge 1 ] || { echo "::error::no submodule members found"; exit 1; }
+          if jq -e 'any(.[]; (.sha | type) != "string" or (.sha | length) != 40)' <<<"$members" >/dev/null; then
+            echo "::error::a submodule has no recorded pin in the tree"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+
+          legs=$(jq -c --argjson skip "$recorded_only" '
+            [ .[] | select(.slug as $s | ($skip | index($s)) | not)
+              | {repo: .slug, ref: .sha, depth: 1,
+                 command: ("test \"$(git rev-parse HEAD)\" = \"" + .sha + "\" && echo \"PIN OK: " + .slug + " @ " + .sha + "\"")}]
+            ' <<<"$members")
+
+          # Coverage assertion: every member is either a
+          # fetch-verified leg or explicitly recorded-only.
+          jq -e --argjson skip "$recorded_only" --argjson legs "$legs" '
+            ([.[] | .slug] | sort) == (([$legs[] | .repo] + $skip) | sort)
+          ' <<<"$members" >/dev/null || {
+            echo "::error::umbrella membership does not match legs + recorded-only; reconcile RECORDED_ONLY in fleet-umbrella-verify.yml"
+            exit 1
+          }
+
+          {
+            echo "## Umbrella pins at ${{ github.sha }}"
+            echo ""
+            jq -r --argjson skip "$recorded_only" '.[] |
+              if (.slug as $s | $skip | index($s)) then
+                "- \(.slug) @ \(.sha) — recorded-only (private member)"
+              else
+                "- \(.slug) @ \(.sha) — fetch-verified"
+              end' <<<"$members"
+          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+
+          echo "jobs=$legs" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          echo "planned $(jq 'length' <<<"$legs") fetch-verified leg(s), $(jq 'length' <<<"$recorded_only") recorded-only"
+
+  verify:
+    name: verify pins via fleet-run
+    needs: plan
+    uses: ./.github/workflows/fleet-run.yml
+    with:
+      jobs: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.jobs }}
+      timeout_minutes: 20
+    secrets:
+      GHCR_ORG_PAT: ${{ secrets.GHCR_ORG_PAT }}
+
+  smoke:
+    name: smoke fleet-build:full
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 15
+    steps:
+      - name: Pull the published image
+        run: docker pull ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full
+      - name: Smoke — the defining toolchain answers (same command the variant pipeline gates on)
+        run: |
+          docker run --rm ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full sh -c 'go version && git --version && jq --version && nix --version'

title: feat(fleet-run): jobs JSON input with parallel matrix execution
body:
Implements Drew's spec for the generic runner: a `jobs` JSON input whose entries execute as a parallel matrix.

## The schema (repos attach per command)

Each entry in `jobs` carries exactly one shape key:

- **Fan-out** — `{"command": "nix flake check", "repos": [{"repo": "developing-today/code"}, {"repo": "dezren39/nix", "ref": "main"}]}` → one leg per repo in the list (the flattened cross product of command × its repos).
- **Together** — `{"command": "…", "together": [{"repo": "developing-today/code"}, {"repo": "developing-today/opencode", "ref": "main"}]}` → exactly ONE leg; all listed repos are cloned side-by-side into `repos/<basename>` and the command runs once from the workspace root. For cross-repo commands; a fan-out entry is the same command independently per repo. Needs ≥ 2 repos (one repo is the flat form).
- **Flat sugar** — `{"repo": "developing-today/code", "ref": "…", "command": "…"}` → exactly one leg.

Every repo object takes an optional `depth` (flat entries: a top-level `depth` on the entry): a positive integer fetches that many commits, `0` fetches full history, absent means 1 — the escape hatch for the rare history work (bisection, archaeology); everything else wants the shallow default. Serial composition is just shell: `cmd1 && cmd2` (or `;`) inside one command string.

## Design

- A lightweight `setup` job (plain runner, 5-minute timeout) resolves the effective leg list and emits it as a matrix output. The `run` job consumes it via `matrix.include` with `fail-fast: false`; each leg is named `run (<repo or label> #<idx>)`, with `idx` assigned after expansion, in order.
- Validation happens in `setup`, on the EXPANDED legs, before anything runs: every repo (including every repo inside `together`) must be one of the five fleet repos; commands must be non-empty; fan-out entries need a non-empty `repos` array; together entries need ≥ 2 repos with distinct basenames; entries mixing shape keys are rejected; `depth`, when present, must be an integer ≥ 0; the expanded leg count is capped at 32 (a together entry counts as 1 leg). Any violation fails the run loudly with the reason.
- Leg execution branches on the leg shape: single-checkout legs are byte-for-byte today's behavior (actions/checkout of the one repo into `target/` with the PAT, now also passing the leg's `depth` as `fetch-depth`); together legs clone each repo with `git clone` in a loop (PAT in the remote URL, masked; `--depth N` when depth ≥ 1, omitted for a full clone; `--branch` when a ref is given), then run the command from the workspace root after echoing the repo → path layout.

## Backward compatibility

With `jobs` empty, `setup` synthesises one flat leg from the existing `repo`/`ref`/`command` inputs — the smoke-proven single-shot path (run 41669880274) is unchanged, including the per-leg timeout clamp expression, which is untouched. One necessary loosening: the `command` input is no longer `required` (a jobs-only dispatch has no single command); if neither form supplies work, `setup` fails with "nothing to run".

## Verification

- The setup resolver was simulated locally against 17 cases: both fan-out forms, flat, together, all three shapes mixed in one array, the single-shot fallback, and every rejection (allowlist, cap at 33 legs, together with 1 repo, mixed shape keys, duplicate basenames, bad repo inside together, empty commands, invalid JSON, negative / fractional / string depths) — all resolve or fail exactly as designed. The together clone loop and run step were likewise simulated (stubbed git for the clone argument shapes across depths 0/1/7 and ref/no-ref; real scratch repos for the layout echo).
- Parse gate: this branch's pushes produced **no** rejection run and the workflow state reads `active` — the same clean signal as the known-good #52 branch; every broken version of this file historically produced a push-event failure run within ~a minute.
- Note: this clone is shared with other fleet automation, which switched the checkout to `main` mid-work; the commit briefly landed on local `main`, was moved onto this branch, and local `main` was reset to `origin/main`. The pushed branch is a single commit on current `origin/main` whose tree is byte-identical to the locally verified file.

Follow-up (parent): a 2-entry matrix dispatch smoke, ideally including one together leg.

Refs: builds on #49/#50/#51/#52.
head: fleet-run-matrix

@@ -5,37 +5,85 @@ name: fleet-run (generic dispatch runner)
 # (publish the images, advance the pins, build one repo's packages);
 # nothing let an agent or a human run an arbitrary build or test
 # inside the fleet's own environment. This workflow is that escape
-# hatch:
+# hatch, in two forms.
+#
+# Single-shot — one repo, one command:
 #
 #   gh workflow run fleet-run.yml --repo dezren39/fleet \
 #     -f repo=developing-today/code -f command='nix build .#mcpx'
 #
+# Matrix — the `jobs` input is a JSON array of entries; the setup
+# job flattens the entries into legs and the legs run in parallel
+# as a matrix (fail-fast is off, so one leg's failure never
+# cancels the others). Entries come in three shapes.
+#
+# Fan-out — repos attach per command; one leg per repo:
+#
+#   {"command": "nix flake check",
+#    "repos": [{"repo": "developing-today/code"},
+#              {"repo": "dezren39/nix", "ref": "main"}]}
+#
+# Flat sugar — exactly one leg:
+#
+#   {"repo": "developing-today/openchamber",
+#    "command": "nix build .#openchamber"}
+#
+# Together — ONE command with several repos cloned side-by-side in
+# the same job, for cross-repo commands (diffing two trees,
+# running one repo's tooling against another's checkout):
+#
+#   {"command": "diff -r code/pkgs opencode/pkgs",
+#    "together": [{"repo": "developing-today/code"},
+#                 {"repo": "developing-today/opencode", "ref": "main"}]}
+#
+# A together entry is exactly one leg regardless of repo count
+# (it needs at least two repos — one repo is the flat form). Its
+# repos land in repos/<basename> under the workspace root and the
+# command runs once, from the workspace root, with all of them
+# present. Use fan-out when the same command runs independently
+# per repo; use together when the command needs several repos at
+# once. An entry carries exactly one of repos / together / repo.
+#
+# In every shape ref is optional (blank = the repo's default
+# branch). Every repo object also accepts an optional depth (on
+# the entry itself for the flat form): a positive integer fetches
+# that many commits, 0 fetches the full history, absent means 1 —
+# the escape hatch for the rare history work (bisection,
+# archaeology); everything else wants the shallow default. The
+# setup job validates the expanded legs before
+# anything runs: every repo must be one of the five fleet repos,
+# and the total leg count is capped at 32. Serial composition
+# needs no machinery of its own — it is just shell: put
+# `cmd1 && cmd2` (or `cmd1; cmd2`) in one command string.
+#
 # Guardrails, such as they are, are structural: the workflow only
 # runs on workflow_dispatch (dispatching requires write access to
-# this repo), the target repo is a fixed five-repo choice, the job
-# timeout is capped at 120 minutes, and the command runs verbatim
-# with its full log on the run page — nothing is hidden or cached
