title: fix(fleet-run): clamp timeout_minutes via fromJSON ternary chain
body:
Line 75 of `fleet-run.yml` has failed three times now, each failure annotated by GitHub itself. This PR is the fourth shape of that line — the original ternary, with only the fall-through branch coerced through `fromJSON` — and the diff is exactly that one line. The Validate-inputs step is unchanged.

## The three annotations, in sequence

**1. The original ternary — parsed fine, failed at evaluation** (dispatch run [41667050628](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/41667050628), main @ 3425f83):

> Error when evaluating 'timeout-minutes' for job 'run'. .github/workflows/fleet-run.yml (Line: 75, Col: 22): Unexpected value '60'

Dispatch inputs reach expressions as strings, and the fall-through of an `&&`/`||` chain returns the raw operand — so `timeout-minutes` received the string `'60'` where a number is required.

**2. The `* 1` coercion — parse failure** (push run [41667363353](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/41667363353), `fix-fleet-run-timeout` @ df6a551):

> (Line: 75, Col: 22): Unexpected symbol: '*'. Located at position 32 within expression: min(max(inputs.timeout_minutes * 1, 5), 120)

GitHub expressions have no arithmetic operators, so the usual numeric-coercion idiom is unavailable.

**3. The `min`/`max` clamp — parse failure** (push run [41667885754](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/41667885754), `fix-fleet-run-fromjson` @ 4a1faca; repeated on main as run [41668200994](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/41668200994)):

> (Line: 75, Col: 22): Unrecognized function: 'max'. Located at position 5 within expression: min(max(fromJSON(inputs.timeout_minutes), 5), 120)

GitHub expressions have no `min`/`max` functions.

## Why this construction is the one the parser accepts

```yaml
timeout-minutes: ${{ fromJSON(inputs.timeout_minutes) > 120 && 120 || fromJSON(inputs.timeout_minutes) < 5 && 5 || fromJSON(inputs.timeout_minutes) }}
```

- Same ternary skeleton as attempt 1, whose syntax parsed — the only change is the fall-through branch, from the raw string input to `fromJSON(inputs.timeout_minutes)`.
- Every branch yields a number: the literals `120` and `5`, or `fromJSON`'s result. `fromJSON` is a documented GitHub expression function; it parses a string like `"15"` into the number 15.
- Only documented operators are used: `>`, `<`, `&&`, `||`. No arithmetic operators, no `min`/`max`. The clamp literals are non-zero, so the `&&`/`||` short-circuit cannot fall through past a legitimately clamped value.

## Parse-gate evidence

Every invalid push of this file produced a push-event run concluding `failure` within about a minute (runs 41667363353, 41667484063, 41667885754, 41668200994). This branch's push (commit d50c8cd) produced **no run at all**, and the workflow's API state is `active` — for a dispatch-only workflow, the absence of a rejection run is the parse signal. Verified via the Actions API (workflow runs for the branch, plus the workflow state) before opening this PR, so this PR was not opened against a file GitHub is still rejecting.

## Pending

The smoke re-dispatch of `fleet-run.yml` is still pending after this merges: an in-range dispatch should run with its stated timeout, and out-of-range values should clamp to 5/120 with the Validate-inputs step reporting the reason.
head: fix-fleet-run-clamp

files.patch:
@@ -72,7 +72,7 @@ jobs:
     # The input is clamped into range so an out-of-range value can
     # never set an absurd timeout; the validate step then fails the
     # run fast with the reason.
-    timeout-minutes: ${{ min(max(fromJSON(inputs.timeout_minutes), 5), 120) }}
+    timeout-minutes: ${{ fromJSON(inputs.timeout_minutes) > 120 && 120 || fromJSON(inputs.timeout_minutes) < 5 && 5 || fromJSON(inputs.timeout_minutes) }}
     container:
       image: ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full
       options: --user root

title: fix(fleet-run): parse timeout_minutes with fromJSON for timeout-minutes
body:
## What failed

Dispatching fleet-run returns HTTP 422 with this annotation (verbatim):

> Unexpected symbol: '*' … within expression: min(max(inputs.timeout_minutes * 1, 5), 120)

## Root cause

PR #50 tried to coerce the string dispatch input to a number with the idiom `inputs.timeout_minutes * 1`. GitHub Actions expressions have **no arithmetic operators at all** — there is no `*` to coerce with — so the workflow file no longer parses, and every dispatch 422s before any job exists. The coercion idiom was the previous fix's error; this PR replaces it rather than layering on it.

## The fix (one line)

```diff
-    timeout-minutes: ${{ min(max(inputs.timeout_minutes * 1, 5), 120) }}
+    timeout-minutes: ${{ min(max(fromJSON(inputs.timeout_minutes), 5), 120) }}
```

`fromJSON()` parses the input's string form (e.g. "15") into a JSON number, which `min`/`max` accept — the clamp semantics are unchanged. The Validate-inputs step stays exactly as it is and remains the range policeman.

## After merge

Re-dispatch the identical code smoke (`nix build github:developing-today/code#mcpx --no-link`, ref main, 15-minute timeout) that originally exposed the parse failure, to verify the workflow now runs.

title: fix(fleet-run): coerce timeout_minutes to a number for timeout-minutes
body:
## What broke

Both smoke dispatches of the new `fleet-run` workflow failed in seconds with zero jobs started:

- [run 41666805050](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/41666805050)
- [run 41667050628](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/41667050628)

GitHub's annotation, verbatim:

> Error when evaluating 'timeout-minutes' for job 'run'. .github/workflows/fleet-run.yml (Line: 75): Unexpected value '60'

## Root cause

Dispatch inputs arrive as strings. The old clamp expression

`${{ inputs.timeout_minutes > 120 && 120 || inputs.timeout_minutes < 5 && 5 || inputs.timeout_minutes }}`

returns the raw string operand on its fall-through branch, and the `timeout-minutes` evaluator rejects a string — so no dispatch could ever start a job. (Sending `timeout_minutes` as a JSON number doesn't help either: the API 422s, and omitting it hits the same path via the default.)

## The fix

One line — coerce to a number inside the expression, then clamp with min/max:

`timeout-minutes: ${{ min(max(inputs.timeout_minutes * 1, 5), 120) }}`

The `* 1` forces numeric coercion. The Validate-inputs step is unchanged, so an out-of-range request still fails fast with the reason once the job can start.

## After merge

A re-run of the identical smoke dispatch follows the merge to prove the workflow starts end to end.

title: feat: generic dispatchable fleet build/test runner (fleet-run)
body:
## What this adds

`.github/workflows/fleet-run.yml` — a generic, dispatch-only build/test runner for the fleet. Every existing pipeline does exactly one job (publish the images, advance the pins, build one repo's flakes); when an agent or a human needs an arbitrary build or test inside the fleet's own environment, there was nowhere to run it. This is that escape hatch:

```sh
gh workflow run fleet-run.yml --repo dezren39/fleet \
  -f repo=developing-today/code -f command='nix build .#mcpx'
```

## Design

- **Trigger:** `workflow_dispatch` only. No push/schedule/PR triggers.
- **Inputs:**
  - `repo` (choice, required) — one of developing-today/code, developing-today/opencode, developing-today/openchamber, dezren39/nix, dezren39/fleet. A `choice` input, so the platform itself rejects anything outside the five.
  - `ref` (string, optional) — branch, tag, or SHA in the target repo; blank checks out its default branch.
  - `command` (string, required) — run verbatim with `bash -lc` in the checked-out tree, full log streamed to the run page; the step's exit code is the command's.
  - `timeout_minutes` (number, default 60) — the job timeout. The expression clamps it into 5–120 so an out-of-range value can't set an absurd timeout, and a validate step then fails the run fast with the reason.
- **Job:** one job on ubuntu-24.04 in container `ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full` with `--user root` — the published org image with the pinned toolchain, Nix, and the baked cache config (the same image the pipelines publish; public, so the runner pulls it anonymously). The target repo is checked out into `target/` under the workspace.
- **Concurrency:** none, deliberately. Every run gets a fresh runner and container; runs share nothing mutable (the hosted nix caches are content-addressed and append-only), so parallel runs are safe and a group would only serialise them.

## Token / secrets story

- Checkout uses `secrets.GHCR_ORG_PAT` — the classic PAT (repo scope) already on this repo (verified present 2026-11-03). It can read all five fleet repos; this repo's `GITHUB_TOKEN` could only read fleet itself. The workflow's own `permissions:` stays at `contents: read`.
- The image pull needs no secret (public package).
- Commands that must run as the image's nix owner can drop privileges the way the variant legs do: `runuser -u vscode -- env HOME=/home/vscode bash -lc '...'`.

## Guardrails

Dispatch-only (dispatching requires write access to this repo), a fixed five-repo choice, a hard 120-minute cap, and a verbatim command with its complete log on the run page. No artifacts, no extra caching layers, no writes anywhere — the job can only affect the outside world through the dispatched command itself, which is the point of the tool and why dispatch access is the gate.

Opened as the developing.today app while the user token is under a secondary rate-limit block; the app is the fleet's standing alternate actor for exactly this.
head: fleet-run-workflow

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,107 @@
+name: fleet-run (generic dispatch runner)
+
+# A generic, dispatch-only build/test runner for the fleet (Drew,
+# 2026-11-03). The existing pipelines each do exactly one job
+# (publish the images, advance the pins, build one repo's packages);
+# nothing let an agent or a human run an arbitrary build or test
+# inside the fleet's own environment. This workflow is that escape
+# hatch:
+#
+#   gh workflow run fleet-run.yml --repo dezren39/fleet \
+#     -f repo=developing-today/code -f command='nix build .#mcpx'
+#
+# Guardrails, such as they are, are structural: the workflow only
+# runs on workflow_dispatch (dispatching requires write access to
+# this repo), the target repo is a fixed five-repo choice, the job
+# timeout is capped at 120 minutes, and the command runs verbatim
+# with its full log on the run page — nothing is hidden or cached
+# away. There is deliberately no concurrency group: every run gets
+# a fresh runner and container, runs share nothing mutable (the
+# hosted nix caches are content-addressed and append-only), so
+# parallel runs are safe and a group would only serialise them.
+#
+# The job runs in the published org image
+# ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full as root: the pinned
+# toolchain, Nix, and the baked cache configuration are already
+# there. Commands that must run as the image's nix owner can drop
+# privileges the way the variant legs do:
+#   runuser -u vscode -- env HOME=/home/vscode bash -lc '...'
+#
+# Checkout of the target repo uses the classic PAT in
+# GHCR_ORG_PAT (repo scope; it can read all five fleet repos —
+# this repo's GITHUB_TOKEN could only read this one).
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      repo:
+        description: "Target repo to check out and run in"
+        type: choice
+        required: true
+        options:
+          - developing-today/code
+          - developing-today/opencode
+          - developing-today/openchamber
+          - dezren39/nix
+          - dezren39/fleet
+      ref:
+        description: "Branch, tag, or SHA in the target repo (blank = its default branch)"
+        type: string
+        required: false
+        default: ""
+      command:
+        description: "Shell command to run in the checked-out tree (bash -lc)"
+        type: string
+        required: true
+      timeout_minutes:
+        description: "Job timeout in minutes (5-120, fails fast outside)"
+        type: number
+        required: false
+        default: 60
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+defaults:
+  run:
+    shell: bash
+
+jobs:
+  run:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    # The input is clamped into range so an out-of-range value can
+    # never set an absurd timeout; the validate step then fails the
+    # run fast with the reason.
+    timeout-minutes: ${{ inputs.timeout_minutes > 120 && 120 || inputs.timeout_minutes < 5 && 5 || inputs.timeout_minutes }}
+    container:
+      image: ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full
+      options: --user root
+    steps:
+      - name: Validate inputs
+        env:
+          TARGET_REPO: ${{ inputs.repo }}
+          TARGET_REF: ${{ inputs.ref }}
+          TIMEOUT_MINUTES: ${{ inputs.timeout_minutes }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          echo "repo:            $TARGET_REPO"
+          echo "ref:             ${TARGET_REF:-(default branch)}"
+          echo "timeout_minutes: $TIMEOUT_MINUTES"
+          if [ "$TIMEOUT_MINUTES" -lt 5 ] || [ "$TIMEOUT_MINUTES" -gt 120 ]; then
+            echo "::error::timeout_minutes must be between 5 and 120 (got $TIMEOUT_MINUTES)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          repository: ${{ inputs.repo }}
+          ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}
+          token: ${{ secrets.GHCR_ORG_PAT }}
+          path: target
+      - name: Run command
+        env:
+          FLEET_RUN_COMMAND: ${{ inputs.command }}
+        run: |
+          git config --global --add safe.directory '*'
+          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target"
+          echo "HEAD: $(git rev-parse HEAD)"
+          bash -lc "$FLEET_RUN_COMMAND"

title: fix(variant): run the offline-shell smoke as root so runuser can drop to vscode
body:
## What failed

Variant run [41660585676](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/41660585676) cleared the check job, all five strict warm-export legs, and the build job's image builds (the #45 PAT-login fix works — the layer-cache export passed). It then failed at the last step before publish, **"Smoke the :full image locally (toolchain + warmed shell OFFLINE)"**:

- Toolchain check passed: `go1.25.14`, `git 2.51.1`, `jq-1.7`, `nix 2.35.4` from the org-tagged `:full` image.
- The offline shell check died instantly:

```
runuser: may not be used by non-root users
```

The smoke's second `docker run` invokes `runuser -u vscode` to drop into the vscode user for the `nix develop .#fleet --offline` check, but the `fleet-build:full` image's default user **is** vscode (both Containerfile targets end with `USER vscode`, devcontainers base), so the container starts unprivileged and `runuser` refuses. The plain pipeline avoids this because its job containers run with `--user root`; the variant's warm-export legs do the same (`options: --user root`) — only this bare `docker run` missed it.

## The fix

One flag, one line, confined to the smoke step:

```diff
-          docker run --rm -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/code-target:/src" ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full \
+          docker run --rm --user root -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/code-target:/src" ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full \
             runuser -u vscode -- env HOME=/home/vscode bash -lc '...'
```

The container now starts as root so `runuser` can drop to vscode, exactly as the legs and the plain pipeline already work.

The toolchain `docker run` is deliberately **not** changed: it invokes no `runuser`, it passed as the image's default user, and keeping it that way preserves the check's fidelity (it verifies the toolchain as the user a consumer of the image actually gets). No leg, gate, login, or plain-pipeline changes.

Refs fleet#46 (standing issue for the build leg; this run predates the #47 report-job extension, so the failure is being recorded there manually).

+          docker run --rm --user root -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/code-target:/src" ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full \

body:
## The blind spot

Variant run [41652341284](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/41652341284) failed in the **build** job, and nothing recorded it: the report job's `needs` covered only `[check, warm-export]`, and its script filtered the run's jobs to names starting with `warm-export`. The build (and commit-pins) legs were structurally invisible to the standing-issue mechanism, so a manual standing issue had to be created instead: #46 ("fleet-build leg failing: build").

## The change (report job only)

- `report.needs` now includes `build` and `commit-pins`, so the report job waits for their final conclusions instead of racing them (it keeps `if: always() && …`, so it still runs — and stays green — in the all-success case and on upstream failures; run-conclusion semantics are unchanged).
- The jobs-API filter now also selects the plain-named `build` and `commit-pins` jobs alongside the `warm-export (…)` matrix legs. The existing leg extraction yields `build` / `commit-pins` for those names, so they flow through the exact same create/comment/recovery path and title format.
- Downstream jobs that never ran are not recorded: when an upstream leg fails, `build`/`commit-pins` conclude `skipped`, and the loop now skips those rows — the failure is recorded on the leg that actually failed, not re-filed downstream.
- **commit-pins is covered** because it fits the same pattern unchanged (a plain-named job whose conclusion the same jobs-API query already returns); the `skipped` guard is what makes including it safe.

## How #46 is adopted, not duplicated

The standing-issue lookup switched from a token search (`"$leg in:title"`) to an exact-title match over the open `fleet-build-leg` issues. That change is load-bearing for the build leg: every standing title contains the token "build" (from "fleet-build"), so the old search could resolve to a neighbouring leg's issue. The new lookup matches `fleet-build leg failing: build` byte-exactly, so the next build failure/recovery comments on #46 and never opens a duplicate. Behaviour for the five warm-export legs is unchanged (their exact titles matched under the old search too).

Nothing else is touched: check, warm-export legs, build, commit-pins, the gate logic, and the plain pipeline are byte-identical outside the report job.

title: fix(variant): use the org PAT for the build job's layer-cache login
body:
## Evidence

Variant run [41652341284](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/41652341284) (force dispatch, 2026-11-03): check ✓, all five warm-export legs ✓ (strict R2 pushes pass — the cache migration is healed), report ✓, but job `build` failed at step **"Build :full (load locally, do not push yet)"**:

```
#19 exporting cache to registry
#19 ERROR: error writing layer blob: denied: installation not allowed to Write organization package
ERROR: failed to build: failed to solve: error writing layer blob: denied: installation not allowed to Write organization package
```

commit-pins correctly skipped.

## Diagnosis

The build job's only GHCR login before the builds was the repo's `GITHUB_TOKEN`:

```yaml
      - name: Log in for layer-cache access (fleet token)
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

Both local builds export their layer cache to the registry under that identity (`cache-to: type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:buildcache-…,mode=max`). The :base export squeaked through, but the :full build's `mode=max` export also writes the warmed-closure layers — blobs GHCR already holds under the **organization** package `ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build` (placed there by the org mirror) — and GHCR denies the write to the Actions *installation* token: a repo's `GITHUB_TOKEN` can only write packages in its own (`dezren39/*`) namespace. That namespace wall is the entire reason the `GHCR_ORG_PAT` classic PAT exists in this workflow's design; the PAT login was simply placed after the builds (it only guarded the final push steps), leaving every earlier registry interaction — including both `cache-to` exports — on the wrong identity.

## Fix

The build job's first GHCR login now uses the classic PAT (`username: dezren39`, `password: ${{ secrets.GHCR_ORG_PAT }}`), so every registry interaction in the job — layer-cache reads/writes and the gated org push — runs as the identity that can write both namespaces. title: fleet-build export: bounded retries for strict-mode cache pushes
body:
Evidence (commented on #32): variant run 41628624575 failed ALL five legs at the R2 nix-cache push — the workers.dev cache hostname would not resolve inside any job container for the whole ~4-minute window, while resolving fine externally and having worked for the plain pipeline hours earlier. Strict mode correctly refused to publish.

This change makes strict-mode pushes ride out short windows: each hosted-cache push (R2 + Cachix) is wrapped in `run_push`, which in strict mode retries up to 3 attempts with 20s/40s backoff before `push_failed` is allowed to fail the leg. Non-strict behavior is byte-for-byte the old single attempt, so the plain pipeline is unchanged. Longer outages still fail the leg and fall to the variant's 30-minute cadence, with the standing leg issues collecting the record.
head: export-strict-retries

   # default stays non-fatal: the nar-cache is what the image build

+    # workers.dev DNS failure windows tracked on fleet#32) with

+    # runs the command exactly once, as before.
+    if [ "${EXPORT_STRICT_PUSH:-0}" = "1" ]; then

title: fleet-build variant: bash shell in container jobs + report-step fixes
body:
Two shakedown fixes from the variant's first run (41622856530), both root-caused from its logs:

1. **Legs died instantly**: in container jobs the runner executes `run:` steps with `sh`, not bash — the plain pipeline's steps happen to be POSIX-clean, the variant's pin-advance step uses `set -o pipefail` and died with `set: Illegal option -o pipefail` before doing anything. Fix: workflow-level `defaults.run.shell: bash`.
2. **Report step exited 1 despite working**: it created all five standing issues (fleet#35-#39) but posted no comments — it re-searched for the just-created issue (search indexing lags, so the number came back empty), and a trailing `[ -n ... ] &&` test set the step's exit code. Fix: use the created issue's URL directly, guard comments with `|| true`, skip the redundant comment on the creating run (the issue body already links it), and end the step explicitly successful.

title: fleet-build: gated pin-fresh variant (30-min, strict, org-only publish)
body:
The gated variant Drew specified (2026-11-03): keep the fleet's submodule pins fresh on a ~30-minute cadence, publish ONLY on a full pass, and make leg failures visible without issue sprawl.

How it works (details in the workflow header):
1. **check** — compare each warmed submodule's committed pin with its upstream HEAD. All aligned -> the run ends (the short circuit; most runs are this one). Otherwise target revs are computed once and shared.
2. **warm-export** — the five familiar legs, realised against the TARGET pins. No optional legs in this workflow. export.sh gains a strict mode (EXPORT_STRICT_PUSH=1, off by default so the plain pipeline is unchanged): a hosted-cache push that fails — or is skipped for missing credentials — fails the leg, converting the #28/#30/#32 silent-warning mode into a hard gate failure. Variant nar-cache keys carry their own prefix, so a hit can only come from an earlier strict run.
3. **build** — build :base and :full locally, smoke :full in docker (toolchain + code's warmed fleet shell OFFLINE), and only then push — to ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build only, via the classic-PAT secret GHCR_ORG_PAT.
4. **commit-pins** — after a successful publish, advance the pointers on main. Pointer-only commits don't match the plain pipeline's path filter, so no loop.
5. **report** (always) — one standing issue per leg (label fleet-build-leg): failures comment the run link (creating the issue if none is open), a pass comments the recovery. No duplicates.

Once this has run green end to end, the org mirror workflow in developing-today/code is obsolete (publishing is direct) and gets retired.
head: fleet-build-variant

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,329 @@
+name: fleet-build variant (gated pin-fresh)
+
+# The gated, pin-fresh variant of the fleet-build publish (Drew,
+# 2026-11-03). Where the plain pipeline (fleet-build-container.yml)
+# publishes whatever is committed, this one keeps the fleet's
+# submodule pins fresh on a ~30-minute cadence and publishes ONLY
+# on a full pass:
+#
+#   1. check — compare each warmed submodule's committed pin with
+#      its upstream HEAD. All aligned -> the run ends here (the
+#      short circuit; most runs are this). Otherwise the lagging
+#      targets are computed once and shared with every later job.
+#   2. warm-export — the same five legs as the plain pipeline, but
+#      realised against the TARGET pins, with NO optional legs and
+#      STRICT cache pushes (EXPORT_STRICT_PUSH=1 in export.sh): a
+#      leg passes only if it realises AND both hosted-cache pushes
+#      (R2 nix-cache + Cachix) succeed. The silent-warning failure
+#      mode of issues #28/#30/#32 is a hard failure here. Variant
+#      nar-cache entries live under their own key prefix, so a
+#      cache hit can only ever come from an earlier strict run.
+#   3. build — build :base and :full (against the target pins'
+#      closures), smoke the :full image locally, and only then push
+#      — to ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build ONLY, authenticated
+#      with the classic PAT in GHCR_ORG_PAT (GHCR registry auth does
+#      not accept fine-grained PATs or another repo's GITHUB_TOKEN).
+#   4. commit-pins — only after a successful publish: advance the
+#      submodule pointers on main to the targets. A pointer-only
+#      commit does not match the plain pipeline's path filter, so
+#      this never re-triggers it.
+#   5. report (always) — per-leg issue bookkeeping in THIS repo:
+#      one standing issue per leg (label fleet-build-leg); a
+#      failure comments the run link on it (creating it if none is
+#      open), a later pass comments the recovery. No duplicates.
+#
+# The legs' tool container is the plain pipeline's published
+# ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:base — the tool image is not the
+# product; the product of this workflow is the org image + pins.
+
+on:
+  schedule:
+    - cron: "*/30 * * * *"
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      force:
+        description: "Run even if all pins already align"
+        type: boolean
+        default: false
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: fleet-build-variant
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+jobs:
+  check:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    outputs:
+      aligned: ${{ steps.cmp.outputs.aligned }}
+      targets: ${{ steps.cmp.outputs.targets }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          submodules: false
+      - name: Compare submodule pins against upstream HEADs
+        id: cmp
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          targets="{}"
+          aligned=true
+          for spec in "code developing-today/code" "opencode developing-today/opencode" "openchamber developing-today/openchamber" "nix dezren39/nix" "zettel developing-today/zettel"; do
+            set -- $spec; leg=$1; upstream=$2
+            git submodule update --init "$leg"
+            current=$(git -C "$leg" rev-parse HEAD)
+            latest=$(git ls-remote "https://github.com/$upstream.git" HEAD | cut -f1)
+            targets=$(printf '%s' "$targets" | jq -c --arg l "$leg" --arg s "$latest" '. + {($l): $s}')
+            if [ "$current" != "$latest" ]; then
+              aligned=false
+              echo "$leg: pin $current -> upstream $latest"
+            else
+              echo "$leg: aligned at $current"
+            fi
+          done
+          echo "aligned=$aligned" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          echo "targets=$targets" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+  warm-export:
+    needs: check
+    if: needs.check.outputs.aligned != 'true' || inputs.force == true
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 60
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        repo: [code, opencode, openchamber, nix, zettel]
+    container:
+      image: ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build:base
+      options: --user root
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          submodules: false
+      - name: Init this repo's submodule and advance it to the target pin
+        env:
+          TARGETS: ${{ needs.check.outputs.targets }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          git config --global --add safe.directory "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
+          git submodule update --init --jobs 4 ${{ matrix.repo }}
+          target=$(printf '%s' "$TARGETS" | jq -r '.["${{ matrix.repo }}"]')
+          git -C "${{ matrix.repo }}" fetch origin "$target" || git -C "${{ matrix.repo }}" fetch origin
+          git -C "${{ matrix.repo }}" checkout --detach "$target"
+          echo "${{ matrix.repo }} advanced to $(git -C "${{ matrix.repo }}" rev-parse HEAD)"
+      - name: Compute nar cache key from the TARGET lock + warmed shell
+        id: key
+        run: |
+          shell=$(awk -v r="${{ matrix.repo }}" '$1 == r { for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) if ($i != "optional") { print $i; exit } }' containers/fleet-build/warm-manifest.txt)
+          [ -z "$shell" ] && shell=default
+          echo "nar-key=fleet-nar-variant-${{ matrix.repo }}-$shell-${{ hashFiles(format('{0}/flake.lock', matrix.repo)) }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+      - name: Restore nar cache
+        id: nar
+        uses: actions/cache@v4
+        with:
+          path: nar-cache
+          key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.nar-key }}
+      - name: Materialise nix-cache signing key for the export step
+        if: steps.nar.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
+        env:
+          NIX_CACHE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.NIX_CACHE_SIGNING_KEY }}
+        run: |
+          if [ -n "$NIX_CACHE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
+            printf '%s' "$NIX_CACHE_SIGNING_KEY" > /home/vscode/.nix-cache-signing-key
+            chown vscode:vscode /home/vscode/.nix-ca

@@ -85,6 +85,18 @@ while read -r repo col2 col3; do
   out="$(echo "$out" | tail -n 1)"
   echo "export: copying closure of $out to nar-cache"
   nix copy --to "file://$export_dir" "$out" || { echo "export: $repo copy FAILED"; exit 1; }
+  # Strict mode (EXPORT_STRICT_PUSH=1, set by the gated variant
+  # workflow): a hosted-cache push that fails — or is skipped
+  # because its credentials are absent — fails the whole leg. The
+  # default stays non-fatal: the nar-cache is what the image build
+  # consumes, and a cache outage must not fail the plain publish.
+  push_failed() {
+    echo "export: WARNING $1 push failed (non-fatal)"
+    if [ "${EXPORT_STRICT_PUSH:-0}" = "1" ]; then
+      echo "export: ERROR $1 push failed and EXPORT_STRICT_PUSH=1 — failing" >&2
+      exit 1
+    fi
+  }
   # Also push the closure to the fleet's hosted binary cache
   # (developing-today/nix-cache on Cloudflare R2 + Workers), signed
   # with the cache's key, so laptops / Codespaces / other CI pull these
@@ -95,7 +107,10 @@ while read -r repo col2 col3; do
     nix path-info --recursive "$out" | nix store sign --key-file "$NIX_CACHE_SIGNING_KEY_FILE" --stdin \
       && nix copy --to "$NIX_CACHE_UPLOAD_URL" "$out" \
       && echo "export: $repo pushed to nix-cache" \
-      || echo "export: WARNING $repo nix-cache push failed (non-fatal)"
+      || push_failed "$repo nix-cache"
+  elif [ "${EXPORT_STRICT_PUSH:-0}" = "1" ]; then
+    echo "export: ERROR $repo nix-cache push skipped (credentials absent) and EXPORT_STRICT_PUSH=1 — failing" >&2
+    exit 1
   fi
   # Also push the closure to the fleet's Cachix cache
   # (developing-today.cachix.org) — the dual-push split (Drew,
@@ -111,7 +126,10 @@ while read -r repo col2 col3; do
     echo "export: pushing $repo closure to Cachix (developing-today)"
     nix path-info --recursive "$out" | xargs -r nix run "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/$(nix eval --raw "$ctx#fleetNixpkgsRev")#cachix" -- push developing-today \
       && echo "export: $repo pushed to Cachix" \
-      || echo "export: WARNING $repo Cachix push failed (non-fatal)"
+      || push_failed "$repo Cachix"
+  elif [ "${EXPORT_STRICT_PUSH:-0}" = "1" ]; then
+    echo "export: ERROR $repo Cachix push skipped (credentials absent) and EXPORT_STRICT_PUSH=1 — failing" >&2
+    exit 1
   fi
   echo "export: $repo OK"
 done < "$manifest"

title: fleet: bump nix pointer to c196d880 (devShells.fleet + wrangler/cloudflared removal)
body:
The nix pointer sat at 6d02290f, which predates dezren39/nix#1383 (devShells.fleet) — so the publish pipeline's nix leg has been erroring on the missing 'fleet' attribute and the manifest's optional flag swallowed it inside green runs (run 41600076443; visibility issue filed separately).

Bump to dezren39/nix main c196d880: carries devShells.fleet (#1383, closes the #1381 warming gap) and the wrangler + cloudflared removal (#1385). After merge, the publish workflow is dispatched manually (pointer-only changes do not match its path filter) and the nix leg verified from its logs and cache narinfos.

title: fix(fleet-build): include the warmed shell in the nar cache key
body: Fixes #30. The nar cache key was lock-only, so the manifest's switch of dezren39/nix from 'default' to 'fleet' (fleet#29) was silently ignored — run 41598906446 restored the default shell's closure and skipped the export. The key now includes the shell token parsed from warm-manifest.txt (same column export.sh reads). First publish after this merge re-exports every repo once under honest keys; that run is the first true realisation of nix's fleet shell by the pipeline.
head: nar-key-shell

files.patch:
@@ -101,13 +101,19 @@ jobs:
           # workspace — mark it safe.
           git config --global --add safe.directory "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
           git submodule update --init --jobs 4 ${{ matrix.repo }}
-      - name: Compute nar cache key from this repo's lock as committed
+      - name: Compute nar cache key from this repo's lock + warmed shell as committed
         id: key
         run: |
+          # The shell token is part of the key (issue #30): the key used
+          # to be lock-only, so switching the manifest from one shell to
+          # another (nix: default -> fleet) silently kept restoring the
+          # OLD shell's closure and skipped the export entirely.
+          shell=$(awk -v r="${{ matrix.repo }}" '$1 == r { for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) if ($i != "optional") { print $i; exit } }' containers/fleet-build/warm-manifest.txt)
+          [ -z "$shell" ] && shell=default
           if [ "${{ inputs.fresh_build }}" = "true" ]; then
             echo "nar-key=fleet-nar-fresh-${{ matrix.repo }}-${{ github.run_id }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
           else
-            echo "nar-key=fleet-nar-${{ matrix.repo }}-${{ hashFiles(format('{0}/flake.lock', matrix.repo)) }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+            echo "nar-key=fleet-nar-${{ matrix.repo }}-$shell-${{ hashFiles(format('{0}/flake.lock', matrix.repo)) }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
           fi
       - name: Restore nar cache
         id: nar

title: feat(fleet-build): dual-push shell closures to developing-today Cachix
body:
Implements the dual-push split Drew chose 2026-11-02: the export jobs keep pushing every warmed shell closure to the R2 nix-cache (uncapped system of record) and now also push it to the fleet's Cachix cache, developing-today.cachix.org (fast hosted layer, bounded shell set only — bulkier artifacts stay R2-only).

- export.sh: NIX_CONFIG trusts the org Cachix cache as an extra substituter; new non-fatal Cachix push block after the nix-cache push, using the cachix CLI from the fleet's pinned nixpkgs (fleetNixpkgsRev). Cachix skips paths already on cache.nixos.org, so only fleet-specific paths land there. Push auth verified beforehand with a probe path (pushed + narinfo live).
- workflow: CACHIX_AUTH_TOKEN secret passed into the export step and through runuser to the export (secret already set on this repo).
- Containerfile: the image's baked nix.conf trusts developing-today.cachix.org alongside the R2 cache.
- README: cache section documents the dual-push split.

Verification: after merge, a fresh_build dispatch re-realises all shells (bypassing the nar actions/cache, which would otherwise skip the exports) and the export logs + narinfo probes on developing-today.cachix.org confirm the pushes.

title: fix(fleet-build): enable ca-derivations in the image's nix.conf
body:
Refs #20.

One-word fix with a long paper trail: the smoke job's `nix develop --offline` inside the published `:full` aborted on the `LocalStore::queryRealisation_` assertion (run 41559640603). Code's shell closure contains a content-addressed derivation; querying its realisation asserts when the store DB has no realisations table, and that table is only created when the `ca-derivations` experimental feature is enabled. The export jobs have always run with it on (export.sh's NIX_CONFIG, since run 41525338113 diagnosed this); the image's baked nix.conf never got it. This adds `ca-derivations` to the image's `experimental-features`.

title: fix(fleet-build): hand nar closures to build-full via artifacts, not cache restores
body:
Refs #20 (root cause corrected there).

Runs 41556877450 and 41557624484 proved the discriminator: the warm-export jobs run **inside the base-image container** (workspace `/__w/fleet/fleet`) and hit the nar caches fine; build-full runs on the **host** (workspace `/home/runner/work/fleet/fleet`) and gets "Cache not found" for identical keys — with identical restore paths too, so the #21 path fix could not save it. actions/cache versions entries on the resolved absolute paths, which differ between the two environments.

This change splits the two concerns:
- **actions/cache** stays exactly as-is inside the export jobs — container↔container works, and it remains the cross-run accelerator that skips re-realising unchanged locks.
- **The handoff to build-full** now uses run artifacts: each export job uploads `nar-<repo>`; build-full downloads all `nar-*`, verifies each required repo contributed at least one narinfo, and merges them into the build context. The now-pointless submodule init in build-full (it existed only to compute cache keys) is removed.

Made via the GitHub API (no local checkout). Verification is the auto-triggered publish run reaching smoke green.

title: fix(fleet-build): restore nar caches to the exports' save path in build-full
body:
Fixes #20.

Run 41556877450 was the first with all five warm-exports green — and build-full still failed: its cache restores reported "Cache not found" for keys the export jobs had hit minutes earlier in the same run. actions/cache versions an entry by key **plus restore paths**; the exports save `nar-cache` while build-full restored to `restored/<repo>`, so the versions never matched.

Change (workflow only): build-full now restores each repo's cache into `nar-cache` — the exports' save path — and merges it into `containers/fleet-build/nar-cache/` before the next restore, applying the required-repo presence check (at least one narinfo) per restore. Optional repos merge when present and are skipped when not.

Made via the GitHub API (no local checkout). Verification is the re-dispatched publish run reaching smoke.

title: chore(fleet): bump openchamber pointer to the outputs-formals fix
body:
Pointer-only bump: openchamber `b86ac21` → `e67f3c1`.

`e67f3c1` is openchamber PR #1389, the hotfix for openchamber#1387: the fleet pin (#1386) added a `fleet` input to openchamber's flake but its outputs formals had no `...`, so every flake output failed to evaluate. That is what failed the openchamber warm-export in run 41555313761 — the other four exports (code incl. its new lean fleet shell, opencode, nix, zettel) all went green in that run.

Made via the Git Trees API (gitlink update only, no local checkout). After merge, the publish workflow gets dispatched manually to re-run the pipeline against the fixed pointer; the other repos' nar caches are keyed by their lock hashes and will hit, so the re-run should be mostly the openchamber export plus build-full and smoke.

Completes tonight's nixpkgs alignment on the pipeline side.

**Pointers:** code → `3001d37`, opencode → `8c81dee`, openchamber → `b86ac21` — the mains carrying the fleet-pin follows (code #4682, opencode #1470, openchamber #1386).

 export NIX_CONFIG="experimental-features = nix-command flakes ca-derivations
 sandbox = false
 eval-cache = false
-build-users-group =
-max-substitution-jobs = 1"
-# ca-derivations: the crash stack (run 41525338113) is
+build-users-group ="
+# ca-derivations is load-bearing: the crash stack (run 41525338113) is
 # LocalStore::queryRealisation_ asserting on a null prepared statement
 # — the realisations table is only created when the ca-derivations
 # experimental feature is on, and something in code's shell closure
-# queries it. Enabling the feature should create the table at store
-# open instead of asserting at first query.
-# Serialise local builds too (see the nix build call): Nix 2.35.4
-# daemonless crashes with a libstore SQLite assertion
-# (SQLiteStmt::Use, std::terminate) once parallel substitution/build
-# registration starts, in every environment tried (BuildKit, job
-# container as root, as vscode — runs 41516480304..41524189872).
-# Fleet CI never sees it: it uses a daemon-mode install. Warming is
-# cache-keyed and not latency-critical, so serial is acceptable here;
-# if this still crashes, the next step is a daemon-mode export job.
+# queries it. With the feature on, realisation proceeds.
+# History: an earlier mitigation also serialised substitution/builds
+# (max-substitution-jobs = 1, --max-jobs 1). Serial WITHOUT
+# ca-derivations still crashed (41525338113); ca-derivations WITH
+# serial ran 80+ min without crashing but was impractically slow —
+# serial downloads of code's huge shell closure — so that run
+# (41526881852) was cancelled and serialisation dropped. If the
+# assertion returns with parallel jobs, ca-derivations was not the
+# (only) fix and serialisation has to come back in a targeted form.
 
 while read -r repo opt; do
   [ -z "${repo:-}" ] && continue
@@ -52,7 +50,7 @@ while read -r repo opt; do
   echo "export: building $repo default dev shell (lock as committed: $(md5sum "$dir/flake.lock" 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f1))"

   for attempt in 1 2; do
-    if out=$(nix build --max-jobs 1 --accept-flake-config --no-link --print-out-paths "$dir#devShells.x86_64-linux.default" 2>&1); then ok=1; break; fi
+    if out=$(nix build --accept-flake-config --no-link --print-out-paths "$dir#devShells.x86_64-linux.default" 2>&1); then ok=1; break; fi
     # Print the HEAD of the failure (the actual error) — v2 printed only
     # the tail, which was an anonymous stack trace (run 41521687044).
     echo "export: $repo attempt $attempt failed:"; echo "$out" | grep -vE "^[0-9]+# " | head -25

title: fix(fleet-build): enable ca-derivations in warm export
body: Stack-identified fix: `queryRealisation_` asserts because the realisations table is never created without the ca-derivations feature. Enable it for the export.
head: fix/fleet-build-ca-derivations

files.patch:
@@ -21,11 +21,17 @@ mkdir -p "$export_dir"
 # install owned by vscode — use its absolute profile path, and pass
 # the flake settings via NIX_CONFIG (root has no nix.conf of its own).
 export PATH="/home/vscode/.nix-profile/bin:/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH"
-export NIX_CONFIG="experimental-features = nix-command flakes
+export NIX_CONFIG="experimental-features = nix-command flakes ca-derivations
 sandbox = false
 eval-cache = false
 build-users-group =
 max-substitution-jobs = 1"
+# ca-derivations: the crash stack (run 41525338113) is

+# experimental feature is on, and something in code's shell closure
+# queries it. Enabling the feature should create the table at store
+# open instead of asserting at first query.

title: fix(fleet-build): serialise Nix substitution in warm export
body: Characterised in run 41524189872: daemonless Nix 2.35.4 crashes on parallel store registration regardless of user/environment. Serialise the warm realisation (max-substitution-jobs=1, --max-jobs 1). If this still crashes, next step is a daemon-mode export job — noted in export.sh.
head: fix/fleet-build-serial-substitute

files.patch:
@@ -24,7 +24,16 @@ export PATH="/home/vscode/.nix-profile/bin:/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH"
 export NIX_CONFIG="experimental-features = nix-command flakes
 sandbox = false
 eval-cache = false
-build-users-group ="
+build-users-group =
+max-substitution-jobs = 1"
+# Serialise local builds too (see the nix build call): Nix 2.35.4
+# daemonless crashes with a libstore SQLite assertion

+# registration starts, in every environment tried (BuildKit, job

+# Fleet CI never sees it: it uses a daemon-mode install. Warming is
+# cache-keyed and not latency-critical, so serial is acceptable here;
+# if this still crashes, the next step is a daemon-mode export job.

   [ -z "${repo:-}" ] && continue

-    if out=$(nix build --accept-flake-config --no-link --print-out-paths "$dir#devShells.x86_64-linux.default" 2>&1); then ok=1; break; fi

title: fix(fleet-build): libgit2 safe.directory for vscode export
body: Follow-up to #9: libgit2 ownership check as vscode. One line.
head: fix/fleet-build-vscode-safe-dir

files.patch:
@@ -113,6 +113,10 @@ jobs:
           # nix as the store's owner, does this daily without it.
           mkdir -p nar-cache
           chown vscode:vscode nar-cache
+          # libgit2 (Nix's flake fetcher) enforces the same ownership
+          # rule as git: as vscode it refused the root-owned submodule
+          # repos (run 41523275400). Mark them safe in vscode's config.
+          runuser -u vscode -- env HOME=/home/vscode git config --global --add safe.directory '*'
           runuser -u vscode -- env HOME=/home/vscode GITHUB_WORKSPACE="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" \
             bash -lc 'cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" && bash containers/fleet-build/export.sh containers/fleet-build/warm-manifest.txt "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"'

title: fix(fleet-build): export as vscode, surface real errors
body: Hypothesis-driven fix: the libstore SQLite assertion correlates with running nix as root against the vscode-owned single-user store (all failing runs), not with BuildKit (41521687044 was a job container). Export now runs as vscode via runuser; error logging fixed to show the actual failure.
head: fix/fleet-build-export-as-vscode

files.patch:
@@ -105,7 +105,16 @@ jobs:
           key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.nar-key }}
       - name: Realise shells + export closures (skipped on cache hit)
         if: steps.nar.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
-        run: bash containers/fleet-build/export.sh containers/fleet-build/warm-manifest.txt "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
+        run: |
+          # Run the export AS vscode, who owns the single-user Nix
+          # store. Runs 41516480304..41521687044 all realised as root
+          # (or under BuildKit) and died on the same libstore SQLite
+          # assertion ~50-60s into code's shell; fleet CI, which runs
+          # nix as the store's owner, does this daily without it.
+          mkdir -p nar-cache
+          chown vscode:vscode nar-cache
+          runuser -u vscode -- env HOME=/home/vscode GITHUB_WORKSPACE="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" \
+            bash -lc 'cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" && bash containers/fleet-build/export.sh containers/fleet-build/warm-manifest.txt "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"'
 
   build-full:
     needs: warm-export

@@ -38,7 +38,9 @@ while read -r repo opt; do
   ok=""
   for attempt in 1 2; do
     if out=$(nix build --accept-flake-config --no-link --print-out-paths "$dir#devShells.x86_64-linux.default" 2>&1); then ok=1; break; fi
-    echo "export: $repo attempt $attempt failed:"; echo "$out" | tail -5
+    # Print the HEAD of the failure (the actual error) — v2 printed only
+    # the tail, which was an anonymous stack trace (run 41521687044).
+    echo "export: $repo attempt $attempt failed:"; echo "$out" | grep -vE "^[0-9]+# " | head -25
   done
   if [ -z "$ok" ]; then
     [ "${opt:-}" = "optional" ] && { echo "export: $repo FAILED (optional, continuing)"; continue; }

title: fix(fleet-build): safe.directory for container submodule init
body: One-line fix from run 41520691666 (dubious ownership in the job container).
head: fix/fleet-build-safe-directory

files.patch:
@@ -82,7 +82,13 @@ jobs:
         with:
           submodules: false
       - name: Init public submodules (never hatch-personal — it is private)
-        run: git submodule update --init --jobs 4 code opencode openchamber nix zettel hatch
+        run: |
+          # Workspace files are owned by the runner host's uid; git in
+          # the container (root) calls that dubious ownership and
+          # refuses (run 41520691666). This is our own ephemeral
+          # workspace — mark it safe.
+          git config --global --add safe.directory "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
+          git submodule update --init --jobs 4 code opencode openchamber nix zettel hatch
       - name: Compute nar cache key from the locks as committed
         id: key
         run: |
